## Slack in the JS heap tables at the peak (2026-11-10)

Task: PR #330 found that JS tables hold most of the peak RSS of vimeo, redis.io and bsky.app. This task measured how much of the tables is slack, by the rule "fix a table only if its slack is at least 5% of the peak RSS on at least 2 of the 3 sites". No table passed. This change is docs only. The decision and the table are in `docs/decisions.md` ("Slack in the JS heap tables at the peak").

### Method

- A temporary probe (not committed) in `Heap::charge` and at the end of each loader round: at each new high of the accounted heap (in steps of 1 MiB), it read `Heap::footprint()`, counted the holes in each element vector, the bytes that strings would save at one byte for each unit, and the payload capacity of the object slab with no object. It asked `mincore` which whole pages of each slack range were resident. The first version sampled at the end of each loader round only. It missed the peak of one bsky.app run, where the scripts ran outside the loader rounds, so the probe moved into `Heap::charge`.
- Sites: https://vimeo.com/, https://bsky.app/, https://redis.io/. Step file `timeout 30000`, `open URL`, `expect js "document.readyState === 'complete'"`, `shot s`. 3 runs each with the probe. 3 runs each of the base `bare-drive` with no probe, for the peak RSS.
- Base: `50e71ca8cc` (origin/main after PR #331). archMachine, other jobs ran at the same time.

### Slack table

MiB at the peak of the accounted heap, median of 3 runs (all 3 runs gave the same numbers on vimeo and bsky.app; redis.io ranges in brackets), and the share of the median peak RSS.

| Table | vimeo | bsky.app | redis.io |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Peak RSS, base, no probe (range) | 291.2 (288.5 to 293.0) | 199.4 (198.6 to 199.5) | 280.9 (278.6 to 295.3) |
| Accounted heap at its peak | 106.9 | 35.2 | 44.9 (44.7 to 50.2) |
| Elements: used / capacity | 66.3 / 103.9 | 1.09 / 1.84 | 2.28 / 4.12 |
| Elements: capacity over the length | 37.6 (12.9%) | 0.75 (0.4%) | 1.84 (0.7%) |
| Elements: resident part of that (estimate) | 25.0 (8.6%) | 0.54 (0.3%) | 1.84 (0.7%) |
| Elements: holes inside the length | 58.3 (20.0%) | 0 | 0.16 (0.1%) |
| Property slots: used / capacity over the length | 7.87 / 0.90 (0.3%) | 4.86 / 1.10 (0.6%) | 13.3 / 3.62 (1.3%) |
| Dictionary entries: used / capacity over the length | 2.12 / 0.87 (0.3%) | 4.39 / 0.77 (0.4%) | 0.45 / 0.08 (0.0%) |
| Object slab: total / capacity with no object | 46.0 / 17.9 (6.2%) | 11.5 / 0.84 (0.4%) | 46.4 / 18.5 (6.6%) |
| Object slab: resident part of that | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| String units (2 bytes each) / saving at one byte for each unit | 3.65 / 0.98 (0.3%) | 10.6 / 5.30 (2.7%) | 4.48 / 1.39 (0.5%) |
| Index tables, shapes | 1.03, 1.78 | 1.61, 1.83 | 0.11, 1.50 |
| Elements freed by "capacity over 2 times the length and 64 bytes" | 0.01 | 0 | 0 |

- The resident part of the element slack: slack bytes on pages that also hold used elements count in full, plus the whole slack pages that `mincore` reports resident (vimeo 7.0 of 19.7 MiB of whole pages).
- vimeo: 4,551 objects of length 64 or more are over half holes. They hold 58.2 MiB of holes and 90.9 MiB of element capacity (31% of the peak). Most are plain objects with no named properties. The common lengths are 951 (1,475 objects, capacity 1,632 or 1,312), 901 (670) and 801 (598, one shape with named properties). In the lengths from 257 to 1,024, 96% of the elements are holes. A write to index `i` goes into the dense vector when `i` is at most `elems.len() + ELEM_GAP` (1,024).
- The heap of vimeo grows from 4 to 107 MiB in one loader round. No collect runs inside it, so a shrink on collect cannot lower this peak.

### Change

Docs only: `docs/decisions.md` and this section. No table changed, by the rule above. No test was written first, because no code changed.

### Cost

After the final rebase: base `1414387821` (origin/main after PR #334), a fresh `base-build` (with `--release -p bare-stress` too); new = this branch on that commit. All 805 rows of `tools/js/cost_matrix.sh`: 0 over under both allocators, 0 over under one, 0 failed, mean change -0.004% glibc. No row reached the jemalloc rerun. Worst row: `bare-stress run table-many-columns 5000` +0.103%. Main moved three times while the checks ran, and each time the docs conflicted, so the branch was rebased three times. Earlier full runs: base `81a5f771ab` (after #335), 805 rows, 0 over, mean -0.002%, worst `resources_load small 1` +0.326%; base `5b32214102` (after #332), 805 rows, 0 over, mean -0.005%, worst `bare-stress run table-many-columns 5000` +0.103%; base `50e71ca8cc`, 805 rows, 0 over, mean -0.006%, worst `resources_load small 10` +0.131%.

### Keycost

`tools/js/typing/keycost.sh` with the prebuilt `type_load` of each base: on `81a5f771ab`, `#a1` 282.7 M and `#f0` 288.0 M instructions for each key, load and mount 572.5 M, peak RSS 33.2 MiB at 20 keys and 33.4 MiB at 50 keys. On `5b32214102`: 282.7 M and 288.0 M, 33.1 and 33.3 MiB. On `50e71ca8cc`: 282.5 M and 287.9 M, 33.6 and 33.2 MiB. PR #328 did not run keycost. These values are after #328, #331, #332 and #335 (not rerun after #334), and close to the last values (282.2 M and 287.5 M). This branch has no code change, so the branch value is the same binary code.

### Checks

- `tools/drive/public/run.sh` with the branch `bare-drive` of the final tree: pass 48, fail 0, known 0, skip 0, flakes 1 (`nextjs-docs` passed on its second try).
- JS gates (`test262_check.sh`, `exec_diff.sh`) were not run: no file in `crates/js` changed.

### Limits

- The probe reads the heap at its accounted peak, not at the RSS peak. The RSS at the heap peak was 256, 208 and 252 MiB (probe runs), against peaks of 288 to 295 MiB. Parsed scripts and script slots are not in the heap tables.

A dictionary entry is 48 bytes and an element 16, so the dictionary is smaller below one third used. To verify first: the V8 and SpiderMonkey rules for sparse elements, and which vimeo script makes the objects.

## Script slots for repeated text and 64 KiB selectors (2026-11-10)

Two limits of `bare` stopped pages that Chrome loads: `Limit("Scripts")` (eu-europa, substack) and `Host("dom-selector")` (two GitHub pages). Chrome has neither. Final base for the cost check: origin/main `1414387821` (#334), from `base-build`. The branch was rebased on it at the end. Main then moved by documentation only (`c6ab5f99`), so the branch was rebased on that without a new run. Earlier measurements (the first full runs, the `reject` table and the live results) used `1bec71ae9b` (#330) or `ff02f72b56` as base, as the text says.

### Cause found: scripts

A temporary counter in `add_script_kind` (not in the change) logged the caller (`#[track_caller]`), the kind and a hash of each text on `bare-drive` runs of both pages.

| page | adds | by caller | different texts | the most repeated text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| eu-europa | 9,227 | `Browser::run_script` 9,221 (Classic), `eval_modules` 4 (Module), `Function` constructor 2 | 12 | 9,211 times, 39 bytes |
| substack | 4,150 | `Browser::run_script` 4,061 (Classic), `eval_modules` 89 (Module) | 96 | 4,055 times, 39 bytes |

The 39 bytes are `!!(document.readyState === 'complete'` + newline + `)`: the poll of the `expect js` step of `bare-drive` (`crates/drive/src/run.rs:592`). It runs one script for each tick, and a realm keeps every script until it ends. The pages themselves add 12 and 96 different texts. A run is stopped by `Limit("Scripts")` only when the page takes long enough for 4,096 ticks, so the result changes from run to run (substack passed once and failed once on the base build).

### Change

- `add_script_kind` (`eval_scripts.rs`): a classic script with the same text as an earlier one gets that slot. `Interp::script_ids` has 4,096 buckets of 4 bytes (16 KiB, allocated at the first script). The bucket comes from a multiply hash of the text, and a hit needs equal bytes. A text that lands on a used bucket takes it over, so a collision costs one extra slot and never a wrong result. A run still instantiates the code again, so each run makes its own functions and checks its own `let` and `const` names. Modules do not share a slot. A realm at `max_scripts` refuses first (a repeated text too), as before.
- A slot of a small script costs about 1 KB (246 B nodes, 92 B caches, 240 B `Code`, 416 B `Program`, about 10 allocations; measured with 2,000 scripts of 40 bytes). 4,096 slots are about 4 MB.
- `browser.rs`: `max_selector_len` 1,024 -> 65,536. GitHub sends lists of 3,387, 3,497 and 3,987 bytes (`.js-remove-unless-platform, [data-analytics-visible], html[data-a11y-animated-images="system"] img[...] ...`) to `querySelectorAll`. A selector parse is charged 4 steps for each byte. The new-name bound is `name_count + len / 2 + 1 <= max_names` (it was `len`). `sel_cache` holds at most 256 selectors and now also at most 128 KiB of text (`SEL_CACHE_BYTES`).
- `docs/decisions.md`: the limits above, and the lines for #316, #317 and #320 that were missing. The brief said "stream request bodies buffered" for #317. The code does not buffer them: a `ReadableStream` body throws `TypeError` (`browser_fetch.rs:898`). The line says what the code does.

### Tests (each failed on main first)

- `the_same_text_keeps_one_script` (JS): 5,000 runs of one text with `max_scripts: 8`. On main: `limit:Scripts` at run 8. It also checks closures per run, a repeated `let` (`SyntaxError`) and the refusal at a full realm.
- `function_constructor_shares_code_for_the_same_text`: 5,000 `new Function` with one text. On main: `limit:Scripts`.
- `long_selector_lists_parse_and_the_caches_stay_bounded` (bare): a 3,492-byte list works; a list over the cap gives `dom-selector`; a short name table gives `dom-names`; a 40,000-byte parse needs 160,000 steps (`Steps` at a 100,000 budget); the cache never holds more than `SEL_CACHE_BYTES`. On main: `limit:Host("dom-selector")` for the 3,492-byte list.
- `selectors_lookups_and_errors`: a 2,000-byte selector now gives `null`; one byte over the cap gives `dom-selector`. On main the 2,000-byte selector gave `dom-selector`.
- `a_long_selector_ends_only_its_task` uses a 70,000-byte selector now.
- `script_count_source_and_node_limits` used one text twice to fill `max_script_source`. It uses two texts now, since a repeated text adds no source.
- Indirect `eval` has no test of its own: `eval` exists only in the browser layer, and it uses the same `add_script` path as `Function`.

### Cost of a selector parse

`perf stat -e instructions:u` of 21 and of 1 parses (distinct texts, a detached element, difference / 20): a list of `.cN,` entries (62 KB) 33.0 M instructions (about 530 for each byte); a list of `a,` of 64,000 bytes 67.5 M (about 1,050 for each byte, the worst); a list of `a[bN="v"] > c,` (60 KB) 22.7 M (about 380 for each byte). One step costs about 370 instructions in a loop that reads `childNodes.length` (4,000,000 steps, 1.48 G instructions). So 4 steps for each byte.

### Cost (full matrix)

- `tools/js/cost_matrix.sh`, 805 rows, base `1414387821`, run after the final rebase. No row is over +0.5% under both allocators. Mean change -0.039% glibc, +0.040% jemalloc. One row is over under glibc only: `reflect_load keys 1` +0.890% (jemalloc +0.040%). The run before the last rebase (base `81a5f771ab`) had three such rows: `reflect_load keys 1` +0.887% (jemalloc +0.039%), `resources_load small 1` +0.556% (jemalloc -0.016%), `resources_load small 10` +1.279% (jemalloc -0.183%). I did not check whether `resources_load small` runs a changed path (to verify). The run on base `1bec71ae9b` had `reflect_load keys 1` +0.887% and `form_load gates 1` and `10` (+0.655%, +0.699%) over under glibc only, and the same mean. The cause of these glibc-only rows is not found (to verify).
- First attempt, a map of all texts (`FxMap<u64, u32>` with `std` insert): `scripts_load many 10` +0.770% glibc and +0.754% jemalloc, `many 1` +0.522% and +0.340%. That is over under both. Cause: 275 instructions for each distinct add (hash, miss, insert, growth). Structural change: a table of 4,096 buckets, no growth: `many 10` +0.361%.
- Second: the hash of `parse_cache` copies the remainder with `memcpy`, and a refused add (a realm at `max_scripts`) did the lookup. `scripts_load reject` with the same setup on both sides was +1.05% and +1.31%. An own hash (overlapping read of the last 8 bytes) and the limit check before the lookup: `reject 1` +0.20%, `reject 10` +0.23%, `many 1` +0.203%, `many 10` +0.270%.
- The `reject` rows of `scripts_load` do another setup now. The old loop filled the table with 63 runs of `var keep = 1;`, which keeps one slot now and never reaches 64. It ran for 63 minutes at 100% CPU in the first full run (that run was stopped). The example fills with `var keep{i} = 1;`. So the counts of the `reject` rows are not comparable with the base rows. All numbers are `tools/js/instr.sh` (minimum of 3, glibc), instructions:

| row | base, old setup | base code, new setup | new code, new setup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `scripts_load reject 1` | 24,305,998 | 23,659,903 | 23,708,070 |
| `scripts_load reject 10` | 193,469,564 | 185,399,424 | 185,825,555 |

  The matrix, which compares the old setup of the base with the new setup of the new code, gives `reject 1` -0.7% and `reject 10` -1.8% (glibc). That is the setup, not the change. With the same setup on both sides it is +0.20% and +0.23%. The "base code, new setup" binary was built in a separate worktree of origin/main with only the example changed (`/data/bare-tmp/ssl/basepatch`).
- Other gates on the final code: `cargo test --release --workspace` 3,360 passed, 0 failed, 13 ignored (before the last rebase; after it `bare-js` and `bare` pass 2,080 tests). `test262_check.sh` gate ok. `exec_diff.sh` 79 runs, 0 differences. `keycost.sh`: 282.2 M instructions for each key in `#a1`, 287.5 M in `#f0`, peak RSS 32.9 MiB at 20 keys and 33.3 MiB at 50 keys (same as before). `tools/drive/public/run.sh`: 48 pass, 0 fail, 0 flakes.

### Live results

`bare-drive`, `timeout 30000`, `open URL`, `expect js "document.readyState === 'complete'"`, `shot s`. `perf stat -e instructions:u` includes the network wait. Peak RSS from `runs` of the result. Before: main `1bec71ae9b`. After: this branch. One run each (the page timing changes between runs).

| page | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| eu-europa | fail, `Limit("Scripts")`, 3.23 G instr, 42.0 MiB | pass, no console message, 4.69 G instr, 48.5 MiB |

An earlier probe on the base of the first measurement (`ff02f72b56`) gave the same `Limit("Scripts")` failure for eu-europa and a pass for substack.

### Limits

- A realm that holds 4,096 different texts refuses every new text, also a repeated one. The old behavior is the same.
- Two different texts that land on one bucket and alternate in a loop add a slot for each run. The table is not a map of all texts.
- A selector at the cap is parsed once for each text, and uncached after 128 KiB of other long selectors. The 50 times estimate of a parsed selector (about 6.5 MB worst case for the cache) is from node sizes, not a measured peak.
- Eight sites that the plan lists as stopped by `Limit(Scripts)`: only eu-europa and substack were checked here.

- Chrome as an oracle for selector lengths.

## Small DOM gaps and lazy web APIs (PR 2 of task 16, 2026-11-10)

Task: close the small platform gaps that stop real sites, and add `Element.animate`, `Path2D` and a minimal `indexedDB` without moving a cost row. PR 1 (#327) did the async machine and the `d` regexp flag.

### Change

- `HTMLCollection.prototype.item` (nasa): `children`, `childNodes`, `getElementsByTagName`, `getElementsByClassName` and `document.scripts`, `forms`, `images`, `embeds`, `links`, `anchors` still give snapshot arrays. They now inherit from one shared prototype (`browser_gaps::wrap_coll`; the new small gaps are in `browser_gaps.rs`) that inherits from `Array.prototype` and has `item`. The prototype is made at the first call. The array is built with that prototype (`Interp::array_from_proto`). First try used `set_prototype_of`: it sends the array to dictionary mode and `nodelist_load live 10` grew +0.53% (glibc) and +0.58% (jemalloc). Building with the prototype gave +0.11%.
- `HTMLScriptElement.prototype.noModule` (gov-uk): a reflected boolean for `nomodule`, next to `async` and `defer`.
- `document.hasFocus()` (mastodon): always `true`. Choice: the page always has system focus (`browser_focus.rs` already said so), so the window focus state is "focused". It is made at the first read.
- `console.assert` (lemmy, redis): main has it since #334 (console work). This change does not add it; an earlier version of this branch did, and I removed it in the last rebase.
- `StyleSheetList` and `CSSRuleList` have `[Symbol.iterator]` (the one of `Array.prototype`), as `NodeList` has (redis).
- `window.event` (nasa, apnews): an accessor that gives the event of the running dispatch, else `undefined`. `Dom::dispatch` sets it and restores the old value (nested dispatch). A write makes a data property (`[Replaceable]`).
- `Element.prototype.animate` and `Animation` (dailymotion), `Path2D` (twitch), `indexedDB`, `IDBKeyRange` and the other `IDB*` names (bsky) are JavaScript (`crates/bare/src/shims/*.js`). `browser_shims.rs` runs the source as an indirect eval at the first read of one of the names. The heap asks the host for a name only when `Heap::browser_name` lists it (the names `animate`, `Animation`, `Path2D`, `indexedDB`, `event`, `hasFocus` and `IDB*` were added). A realm that never reads them pays for nothing: no script, no object.
  - `animate` returns an `Animation` that ends after one timer: `finished` resolves, then `onfinish` and `finish` listeners run. `cancel`, `pause`, `play`, `finish` change `playState`. `cancel` rejects `finished` with an `AbortError` that is marked handled. No effect, no timeline.
  - `Path2D` has the constructor and the 11 path methods as no-ops.
  - `indexedDB`: `open` (with `upgradeneeded`, `VersionError`), `deleteDatabase`, `cmp`, `databases`; `createObjectStore` (keyPath, autoIncrement), `deleteObjectStore`; transactions (`readonly`, `readwrite`, `versionchange`) that run their requests one by one in microtasks and complete when the queue is empty; `get`, `getKey`, `getAll`, `getAllKeys`, `put`, `add`, `delete`, `clear`, `count`, `openCursor` (with `continue`, `advance`, `update`, `delete`); `IDBKeyRange`. An error aborts the transaction and rolls back its writes. The classes extend `EventTarget`, so `addEventListener` works. Values are copied with `structuredClone`. No persistence and no indexes (`createIndex` is absent).
  - `new DOMException(...)` is not a constructor in this realm (the interface is illegal), so the shims make errors with `Object.create(DOMException.prototype)` plus `name`, `message` and `code`.

Tests (written first, all failed on main): `crates/bare/src/browser_gaps_tests.rs`, 9 tests.

## Host asks and cached prototypes: the target.com `Heap` stops (2026-11-10)

### Problems

https://www.target.com/ stopped with `page stopped: Heap` in 2 of 4 runs of main `5b322141` (plan 7). A heap error that stops a page is an engine bug.

### Backtraces

A scratch build (not committed; `/data/bare-tmp/hs/instrumentation.patch`) logged each host fill and the backtrace of `Interp::herr`. It also lifted the script-count cap, because 6 of 6 runs of `81a5f771` stopped at `Limit(Scripts)` first. 19 runs, logs in `/data/bare-tmp/hs/dbg*/`. 5 stopped at `Heap(NeedsHost)`, 2 at `Heap(Stale)`.

1. `NeedsHost { owner: window, index: LAZY_ON }` (or `owner: <frames object>, index: u32::MAX - 8`): `herr` <- `set_miss` <- `put_prop` <- `member_put_ic` <- `ref_put` <- `eval_assign`. The write is `window.onDvtagReady = ...`. The fills before the error: the frames object (`browser_frames::FILL`), `EventTarget.prototype` (`LAZY_ON`), `window` (`LAZY_ON`). That is 3 asks, and the evaluator allowed 2.
2. `Stale`: `herr` <- `heap_error` <- `Dom::wrap` <- `make_element` <- `create_element`. The element is `walrus` (an unknown HTML name). Its prototype (`HTMLUnknownElement.prototype`, a high object index) was dead.

### Causes

1. The frames object on the chain of `window` (`browser_frames.rs`, named iframe access) walked the tree for each named query. It charged the walk in prepaid groups of 8 and asked the host again each time the 8 ran out. So its ask was not once for each name, and it could come in any repeat of an operation. A write of an `on<x>` name to `window` also asks `EventTarget.prototype` and `window`. With an iframe in the page and a balance under 3 at the start of the write, the write needed 3 asks.
2. `Dom::ce_roots` (`browser_custom.rs`) returned before it added `ce.unk` (`HTMLUnknownElement` prototype and constructor) and `ce.int` when the page had not used the custom element registry. A collect freed them while `ce.unk` still held them. The next unknown element got the dead prototype.

The plan's hypotheses were not the causes. The lazy asks of one `(object, name)` pair stay once each. `Dom::wrap` cannot meet a collect between making a wrapper and its insert (a collect runs only when no call is active). The `by_node` maps of `browser_cssom.rs` and `browser_shadow.rs` hold permanent roots and pruned wrappers.

### Tests that failed first

`crates/bare/src/browser_heap_stop_tests.rs` (log: `/data/bare-tmp/hs/tests-on-main.txt`):
- `writes_of_on_names_to_window_with_an_iframe_never_stop_at_the_heap`: 40 writes `window['onzz' + i] = i` on a page with an iframe and 40 divs. On main: `other:Heap(NeedsHost { owner: ObjId { index: 3, gn: 0 }, index: 4294967294 })`.
- `cached_wrapper_prototypes_survive_a_collect`: one element for each cached prototype of `Dom::wrap` (30 kinds), a collect, then the same again. On main: `other:Heap(Stale)`.
- `named_iframe_access_follows_the_tree` (new iframe, renamed iframe, removed iframe, `window.length`, `Object.keys`) passed on main and passes now. It guards the new frames list.

### Change

- `browser_frames.rs`: the frames object keeps its iframe list, its keys and a map from name to iframe for one document revision (`Document::revision`). A query reads only the list. When the list is out of date, the query asks once. The fill builds the list, charges one step for each node of the document, and makes the context of the asked name. The prepaid count (`paid`) is gone.
- `eval.rs`: `MAX_FILLS = 3` replaces the bound 2 in `hx!`, `hxw!`, `get_miss`, `set_miss` and in `heap_miss` and `heap_miss_w` (`eval_proxy.rs`). Its comment lists the sources of asks and why one operation asks at most 3 times. The code of the fast path is the same.
- `browser_custom.rs`: `ce_roots` adds `ce.unk` and `ce.int` before the early return.
- `lib.rs`: one test module line.
- `docs/decisions.md`: "One property operation asks the host at most three times" and "Every prototype that the host caches is a root".

### Cost

- Final: `tools/js/cost_matrix.sh -J`, 805 rows, BASE `f857a90b71` (fresh `base-build` of main after #333), NEW this branch after the final rebase, both allocators on every row. 0 rows over +0.5% under both, 0 over under one. Mean change -0.011% glibc, +0.006% jemalloc. Logs: `/data/bare-tmp/hs/matrix-final2.txt`, `.raw`. The merge queue (`merge-gate`) held main during the final checks.
- An earlier full run on base `8f6a38e982` (before #333 merged): 0 over under both, mean -0.001% glibc, +0.008% jemalloc. Over under jemalloc only: `form_load gates 1` and `10` (+0.633%, +0.701%; glibc +0.407%, +0.432%).
- `keycost.sh` (final): BASE `f857a90b` 283.1 M for each key in `#a1`, 288.5 M in `#f0`, peak RSS 33.5 / 33.5 MiB at 20 / 50 keys. NEW 283.1 M, 288.5 M, 33.4 / 33.3 MiB.

## Sparse element writes on plain objects

The regression test creates 1,000 objects with 30 integer keys spread over 0 to 950. On base `8f6a38e982`, element capacity was 16,896,000 bytes. The new bound is 128,000 bytes. The semantic and collect tests passed on the base. The capacity test failed first. Logs: `/data/bare-tmp/se/tests-before.log` and `tests-after.log`.

The scratch probe found a far write at `script#74:1:130774` (index 2076, old length 1432). The palette maps appear at `script#86:1:3760`, including red keys 100 and 500. Source: `https://f.vimeocdn.com/cms/_next/static/chunks/5121-163c7299a2c24cfc.js`. The maps use numeric shade and spacing keys. The repeated writes at `script#83:1:172461` include 100, 200, 300, 550, 800 and 900. The trace is `/data/bare-tmp/se/probe/trace.log`. The probe was removed before the implementation build.

The rule checks density only when a plain object's element vector grows by more than 16 slots. At least one quarter of the proposed slots must hold values. Each decision scans at most 4,096 slots; accounting and storage together scan at most 8,192. Arrays, objects with named properties, and existing vectors longer than 4,096 slots keep the old rule. Named reads in a local workload rose by 2.54% without the exemption and 0.08% with it. Array append, forward fill and reverse fill changed by +0.15%, +0.15% and -0.04% in the first measurement. Inputs and counts: `/data/bare-tmp/se/fill-cases.txt`, `fill-bench.log`, `fill-bench-2.log`.

### First final validation and stop (superseded)

The branch stayed unmerged after the first validation. That matrix passed, but reverse fill rose by 1.257%. Redis also failed to reach readyState in the NEW live run. ### Limits and not tested

Objects that later gain a named property can already be in dictionary mode. The rule does not restore their shape. Gaps of at most 16 and existing vectors longer than 4,096 slots can still hold many holes. Arrays keep the existing storage policy, but the reverse-fill cost above still rose.

Not tested: repeated live pairs for the six sites other than vimeo; Chrome as a performance oracle; sparse-to-dense migration. The CSS failure and the extra theverge error were not isolated. The reverse-fill regression was not fixed. No hunks owned by other executors were changed.

## Task 32: pending shorthand scope investigation (2026-11-10)

The twitch stop remains unfixed. This section records the reviewable fallback required by the task. No implementation change or scope expansion was made.

### Trigger and source

BASE: `d8550bbba0`. The initial rebase was up to date. Live ownership diffs were checked before edits. Scratch diagnostics changed only `browser_style_block.rs` and were removed from the branch.

Two diagnostic runs stopped at the same `Unsupported` error. The second backtrace shows `browser_cssom::insert`, `parsed_rules`, `new_rule`, the internal `cssText` setter, then `serialize`. The page operation is `CSSStyleSheet.insertRule`. It is not a separate page assignment to a corner longhand. The internal declaration text includes `border-radius:var(--button-border-radius-large);border-top-left-radius:0;border-bottom-left-radius:0;`. Both surviving right corners still belong to the pending shorthand. The complete input and backtrace are in `/data/bare-tmp/cvl/twitch2-stderr.txt`.

Fetched scripts were data only. The button template is in `https://assets.twitch.tv/assets/39247-947dcb7a9cc679940650.js`, zero-based character offset 3499 for the template area (the variable token occurs at 4185). It emits the radius followed by four conditional corner declarations. The stylesheet adapter calls `this.sheet.insertRule(t,e)` in `https://assets.twitch.tv/assets/34609-36d2f7024ebdf95896ac.js`, at offset 620930 for `.insertRule(`. The live backtrace proves the native operation. These fetched positions identify matching source, not a captured JavaScript stack position.

### Rule and scope boundary

CSS Variables 1 section 3.2 requires pending longhands to retain their source shorthand until computation and serialize as empty values. CSSOM defines declaration order and serialization. Sources are linked in the decisions entry. The browser oracle used a fresh blank preview tab, which was closed after the check. Its observations are retained in `/data/bare-tmp/cvl/oracle.json`.

With `--m: 3px 4px; margin: var(--m)`, writing `marginTop = '1px'` produced `margin-top: 1px; margin-right: ; margin-bottom: ; margin-left: ;`. Order stayed top, right, bottom, left. The right computed margin stayed `4px`, then became `8px` after `--m: 7px 8px`. Removing the left margin made its computed value `0px`. Copying the serialized text lost the pending right and bottom margins. This is an observed lossy round-trip, not a proposed invariant.

`browser_style.rs` writes serialized text to the attribute and caches only a parse-equivalent block. `crates/css/src/cascade.rs` computes inline styles from attribute text. A correct fix needs persistent pending state and a route from that state into computation. The allowed serializer and a tiny CSSOM caller change cannot supply that route for element writes and removal. No empty-value drop, whole-shorthand resurrection or early substitution was implemented. The decisions entry describes the precise follow-up requirement. These files remain owned or off limits.

### Checks and retained evidence

- Diagnostic build: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/bare-tmp/target-cvl /data/bare-tmp/bin/heavy cargo build --release -p bare-drive`. Logs: `diagnostic-build.txt`, `diagnostic-build2.txt` under `/data/bare-tmp/cvl/`.
- Live probe: `/data/bare-tmp/bin/heavy timeout 75 /data/bare-tmp/target-cvl/release/bare-drive --out /data/bare-tmp/cvl/twitch2 /data/bare-tmp/plans/p9chk/out/twitch/steps`. Readiness failed with the original stop. Logs: `twitch2-stdout.json`, `twitch2-stderr.txt`. The first run took 4840.6 ms with peak RSS 266724 KiB. The second took 2963.1 ms with peak RSS 268924 KiB. Both logged the fatal page error; the second also reported a refused analytics connection. These diagnostic runs are not a performance comparison.
- Tests-first: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/bare-tmp/target-cvl /data/bare-tmp/bin/heavy cargo test --release -p bare --lib pending_reduction`. Three scratch unit cases for overwrite, removal and priority failed at serialization before any fix. `tests-first.txt` retains output. All four cases failed in a second run on the unmodified implementation, including the reduced stylesheet insertion. Source: `reduction-tests.rs`; output: `tests-unmodified.txt`. Scratch tests are not committed as a permanently failing suite.
- `base-build origin/main --release -p bare-drive` returned `/data/bare-tmp/base/d8550bbba0/target`. Log: `base-build.txt`. A scratch local-file drive probe was invalid because drive accepts HTTP(S) document URLs. It is not page evidence; the reduced browser unit test replaces it.

## Task 33: pending shorthand state and cascade integration (2026-11-10)

### Approval, problem and change

The owner approved style-state and computed-style/cascade integration on 2026-11-10 for the scope identified by draft #339. This approval supersedes Task 32's scope hold and the earlier interim Task 33 entry. The fix is now implemented. No cost waiver or budget increase was requested.

Twitch inserts a rule with a variable border radius and two left-corner overrides. Serialization previously stopped because the surviving pending corners have no exposed longhand value. Empty text alone cannot preserve their source for computation. Redis intermittently reaches the same guard.

The serializer now reports pending output and exposes empty longhand values. A separate bounded store retains source shorthand, surviving mask, priority and order across element writes. Attribute spans invalidate state on replacement, including equal text. The ordinary parse-cache block keeps its original fields. Pending storage is boxed and remains independent of cache eviction and wrapper lifetime. Existing style object, byte and declaration caps bound it. Retained-source copying and parsing remain charged.

RuleSet accepts masked inline and published CSSOM inputs. It substitutes variables during computation. Removed members remain removed. Copying cssText remains lossy. A compile-time path selects retained-input handling before the node loop. The ordinary loop keeps its text representation and has no retained-state lookup. RuleSet grew from 560 to 568 bytes; the standalone size probes are in `sizes-{base,new}.txt`. Per-sheet text identity is tracked only for sheets with retained state. An unrelated sheet keeps its rule objects when another element creates pending state.

## BBC and Dailymotion split attribution (Task 35)

Evidence-only. Frozen main: `617cb19f8984a6781e5e31a4655e3d598f705d17`. Artifacts: `/data/bare-tmp/bst11/`. These paths are local evidence, not hosted PR attachments. Only this section and a decisions entry change. Tests-first is N/A for this documentation change. No matrix ran.

### Independent source attribution

BBC: `https://gn-web-assets.api.bbc.com/ngas/latest/dotcom-bootstrap.js`, downloaded decoded SHA-256 `07ff68d400013493a7f221a0fe9a9bff82ca0fc2f854752c0ad75e9396fc5ef3` (76067 bytes). `dn` checks `window.dotcom.userinfo.notUkIp` and `.ads`, calls `k.checkCookies()`, then `oe()`. `oe` reads `window.location.pathname`, `.hostname`, `.search`, optional `window.SIMORGH_DATA.pageData.metadata.type`, and `window.dotcom.config.adCampaign/topics`. It then evaluates `document.referrer.split("https://www.bbc.com/")`. The receiver is `document.referrer`. Failure there prevents the later assignment to `window.dotcom.data`, including referral targeting keys. The source explains a bootstrap rejection, not a fatal page stop. The live signature is `Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split') at script#55`. The console does not map that script number to a URL or provide the receiver. Hypothesis: this source path is the live rejection. No instrumented live stack establishes that mapping.

Dailymotion has two relevant source paths. Its downloaded document `https://www.dailymotion.com/` contains inline script 7 with startup `landing.referer: window.document.referrer.split("?")[0].slice(0,100)||void 0`. Before this read, startup reads runtime configuration, location search and visit data. Failure prevents publication of the initial app-enter event. The same inline bundle has `getLanding()`: `this.referrer=this.referrer||window.document.referrer.split("?")[0].slice(0,100)`. Its receiver is again `window.document.referrer`, after reading the cached `this.referrer`. A failure prevents return of landing tracking data.

The external application bundle repeats `getLanding`: `https://static.neon-ssr.dailymotion.com/neon-user-ssr/static/app.28f908af5c3132ac5a4b.js`, decoded SHA-256 `baa699ab89ece2be1d33dc282b6a9a8c8e520acd70450119df2bca1fc86392a4` (133871 bytes). Module 23190 builds an event with `getAppInfo()`, `getLanding()`, then device/visitor/browser/player reads; it sends the event only after those calls. The live signature is `listener of error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')`. Hypothesis: the listener reaches this tracking path. The raw console lacks a stack. The initiating error and exact live listener call path remain unverified. Do not equate this listener exception with BBC's promise rejection or with player failure.

Source files, URLs, decoded hashes and sizes are retained in `scripts.json`, `scripts/`, `bbc.html`, `dm.html` and `dm-inline-7.js`. ## Mastodon constructor attribution (Task 36)

Documentation only. Frozen main is `617cb19f8984a6781e5e31a4655e3d598f705d17`. Artifacts are in `/data/bare-tmp/mct11/`. They are machine-local, not hosted attachments. Exact edited files: `docs/decisions.md` and `docs/progress.md`. Read every worktree's status and branch diff before work and before edits; retained the latter in `owners-before-edit.txt`. Task 35's `bbc-split-trace` worktree had no changes at that check. The required runtime registration is in excluded, Task 24-owned `browser.rs`. No implementation is attempted.

### Source and value attribution

The retained p9chk, p10chk and p11chk Mastodon results all contain `Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: y is not a constructor at script#3:2:11455`. Two fresh readiness probes reproduce that exact text on frozen main. Preserve the separate `listener of error: TypeError: y is not a constructor` and worker-script warning; neither is a new constructor failure.

Downloaded source: `https://mastodon.social/packs/polyfills-DNX-ejKw.js`, 60,721 decoded bytes, SHA-256 `0bda73b061cef806d2f11d395d8a54ee0bd7cc0655de2a1c4ca9e472ba8261e1`. Column 11455 on line 2 begins `new y(1,2)`. The enclosing module is `At`; its declarations include `_ = 'DOMException'`, `i = g()`, `y = i(_)`, and `C = 'stack' in new y(1,2)`. The `g` helper reads `r[e]` from the global object and returns it if callable. The global helper selects `globalThis`, then window/self fallbacks. Thus `y` is the host's global `DOMException`, not a guessed minified binding. The earlier `new y(t, ...)` occurs inside an uncalled wrapper; the top-level stack probe is the failing expression.

At frozen main, `browser.rs` registers `("DOMException", domexc, None)`. The `None` interface path uses `add_fn(... illegal_constructor, ..., false)` rather than `add_ctor_nt`. A callable interface exists, but it lacks construction support. `Dom::dom_err` separately creates exception-like objects; its presence does not implement the public constructor.

Minimal reduction (`repro.html`, served over loopback by `reduce.py`):

```js
var y = globalThis.DOMException;
console.log('source', typeof y, y === window.DOMException);
try { var C = 'stack' in new y(1, 2); console.log('constructed', C); }
catch (e) { console.error(e.name + ': ' + e.message); }
```

Frozen main prints `source function true` then `TypeError: y is not a constructor`. The HTTP reduction exits 0 because it catches the exception; this is diagnostic evidence, not a passing constructor regression. The initial local-path probe failed because bare-drive requires HTTP(S); retain `repro/` and the corrected `repro-http/` outputs. The loopback server is stopped by the reduction script.

[Web IDL DOMException](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMException) defines a constructor with optional DOMString message and name, defaulting to empty message and `Error`. For `(1,2)`, conversion gives message `"1"`, name `"2"`, code 0. The call must construct an exception; the standard does not require a `stack` property. A Node check returns `{"name":"2","message":"1","code":0}` (`node-oracle.txt`). Retain `webidl.html` as the consulted source. No browser oracle was run.

No foreign worktree was edited.

### Source, receiver and feature

Downloaded `https://angular.dev/main-47UB4TBV.js`: 621365 decoded bytes, SHA-256 `5b26e63417ebbb7a428898874806e61f1af21e987be15af4c24a2f4facfe2c41`. File `scripts/3.js`; source manifest with all downloaded resource URLs, sizes and hashes: `scripts.json`. Downloads are fresh source captures, not retained bodies from the older probe. Source scan: `source-reads.txt`; command: `python3 /data/bare-tmp/alt12/download.py`.

The constructor for class `et`, selector `docs-icon`, reads `let a=D($t)` and schedules `zu(async()=>{t.whenFontLoad??=a.fonts.load('normal 1px "Material Symbols Outlined"'),await t.whenFontLoad,t.isFontLoaded.set(!0)})`. The receiver of load is `a.fonts`. The assignment starts at decoded character offset 139790, line 503, column 12334. The main imports `D` as export C, `$t` as export a and `zu` as Gi from `chunk-CS9qujL_.js`. That chunk defines D as injector access and zu as the NgAfterNextRender registration. The import token is also used by the bundle's `_document` fields. Hypothesis: `a` is the application document. The fixture below verifies the host document read independently; no live receiver identity was captured.

The component starts `isFontLoaded` false. Its `fontSize` computed value is zero until that signal becomes true, and its host binding writes font-size in px. Thus the concrete source feature is icon-font visibility after rendering. Rejection before assigning the cached promise leaves later constructors able to try again. Hypothesis: this explains the repetition. Twelve errors do not prove twelve constructor instances. Search functionality and whole-page hydration were not exercised or established as broken by this error.

### Fresh runs and reduction

Build command: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/bare-tmp/target-alt12 /data/bare-tmp/bin/base-build 1b9bff1d912bb17852eb3b99b01a80820d7838fb --release -p bare-drive`. Live probes use `timeout 75`, the retained p12 Angular steps, 30000 ms readiness timeout, and `shot s`.

Both p11chk and p12chk retained Angular results contain twelve `Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'load') at script#6` entries. Both fresh runs repeat that signature twelve times. Run 1: ready true, exit 0, 1344.3 ms, peak RSS 86076 KiB. Run 2: ready true, exit 0, 1537.1 ms, peak RSS 89748 KiB. Neither reports a driver failure, fatal stop, task stop or failed network resource. All transferred resources and console entries remain in `angular-1/stdout.json` and `angular-2/stdout.json`, with steps, stderr, screenshots and exit codes. The main JS transfers 105317 bytes in each run; decoded source size differs from transfer size. No application sentinel or interaction was asserted. Readiness does not establish application success.

The later `Error: WebAssembly is not defined` remains separate at script#7:36:77664, followed by script#7:36:74646 and script#7:3:33683. Run 1 records it once; run 2 twice. Task 37 owns that capability investigation. Matching chronology is not evidence of causality.

Minimal executed fixture (`reduction.html`), served over ephemeral loopback HTTP:

```html
<!doctype html><docs-icon>search</docs-icon><script>
let a = document;
console.log('fonts receiver', typeof a.fonts);
(async () => { await a.fonts.load('normal 1px "Material Symbols Outlined"'); console.log('font completed'); })();
</script>
```

The reduction exits zero with readiness true, logs `fonts receiver undefined`, then the same promise TypeError at script#1. It does not log font completed. Result: `reduction.json`, stderr: `reduction.err`, runner: `run.py`, complete run output: `run.log`. It takes 11.0 ms with peak RSS 13100 KiB. The only resource is the HTTP 200 fixture. The server closes before the runner exits. This isolates a host-value failure without WebAssembly, network app data or a framework dependency. It does not prove the live script-number mapping.

### Checked local candidate, not included

Read `eval_stack.rs` and `Heap::get` before implementation. The former stores `Error.stack` as an own data string at construction. It contains actual function names, script slots and available line/column positions. It omits URLs and unavailable positions. The latter returns `Get::Accessor` without invoking user code. `Dom::error_text` already reads data properties and truncates decoded UTF-16 at `min(max_string_bytes,4096)` UTF-8 bytes.

The candidate reuses that bounded machinery. A nonempty data-string stack replaces the diagnostic header; it does not duplicate it. Missing, empty, accessor and nonstring stacks fall back to name/message. The window ErrorEvent still receives the existing message and thrown value. No frame capture, new field, lazy-name token, scheduler production edit or interpreter edit is required. The candidate reads diagnostic text before window error handlers run. It retains report accounting and recursion protection.

Tests-first: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/bare-tmp/target-csr14 /data/bare-tmp/bin/heavy cargo test --release -p bare --lib callback_report` fails all three initial regressions on frozen main (`failing-first.log`). The named listener and timer reports lack their real stored frame. The Unicode report retains only `Error: unicode`. The same command after the candidate passes four tests (`targeted.log`); the fourth adds an empty-stack and zero-report-cap guard and was not run failing-first. Checks cover real named frames, unchanged ErrorEvent text, later listener/timer execution, plain string throws, missing/nonstring/accessor stacks without getter execution, empty stacks, Unicode truncation to 128 bytes, bounded report retention, drop counts and recursive error-handler refusal. The saved candidate also changes four old assertions in the allowed handler/scheduler files to compare the unchanged first line.

Candidate patch: `/data/bare-tmp/csr14/candidate.patch`. It is evidence for a follow-up, not shipped code. `commands.txt` retains commands and frozen identity. The redundant direct test and binary-build requests were stopped while waiting for slots after selecting documentation only; neither produced a result. Their empty logs are not passing checks.

## Lazy document fonts and FontFace (Task 40)

Angular's icon callback received undefined from document.fonts. The owner authorized a minimal FontFace class and a bounded font set. Font loading resolves in memory. It makes no font request and decodes no font data. The source mapping of the live receiver remains a hypothesis from Task 38.

### Scope and implementation

New files: browser_fontface.rs, browser_fonts.rs and browser_fonts_tests.rs. The existing basics dispatcher exposes fonts and FontFace lazily. The heap adds only those two exact names. Module registration changes are local. No host field, new heap hook, eager getter, install function, event surface or CSS change is added. A page that reads no font API creates no font source, method or state. The focused test checks that both lazy properties remain absent after ordinary document reads.

Private weak maps brand faces and sets. Captured collection methods preserve brands after prototype writes. Native Set storage supplies entry limits and live mutation during forEach. A native document check and weak cache isolate sets for each document, including createHTMLDocument results. Repeated document.fonts and ready reads keep their identity. Family, source and descriptors convert to strings. Missing constructor arguments throw TypeError. A face starts unloaded. Its load method marks it loaded and resolves its stable loaded promise with itself. Set load selects stored faces by family and resolves an empty array when none match. Check returns true after conversions and shorthand validation. No glyph availability is established.

## Cross-platform core: plan and topic 1 (2026-11-10)

Owner request: build `bare` as a cross-platform product, with a core that does not depend on the OS. The first use is a headless MCP server for end-to-end tests (branch `mcp-server`, held until this topic merges). The decision and its rules are in [decisions.md](decisions.md#cross-platform-core-owner-decision-2026-11-10).

### Inventory on main (13c6b0bc, after #366)

- Window: `bare` always depended on `bare-window`, and `bare-window` always built Wayland (`smithay-client-toolkit`, `rustix`, `std::os::unix`). A Windows build of `bare-drive` failed there.
- Random bytes: `tls/random.rs` reads Linux `getrandom` or `/dev/urandom`. Other OSes return `Unsupported`, so TLS fails. `Math.random` seeds from `/dev/urandom` (`js/eval_numeric.rs`).
- DNS: `net/dns.rs` reads the servers from `/etc/resolv.conf`.
- Trust roots: `tls/trust_store.rs` reads Linux bundle files under `/etc/ssl` and `/etc/pki`.
- Time zone: `js/eval_intl.rs` reads `TZ`, then the `/etc/localtime` link, and the zone data under `/usr/share/zoneinfo`. Windows has none of these.
- Counts: CPU time and memory from `/proc` (`bare/main.rs`, `drive/run.rs`, `drive/main.rs`, `bench/main.rs`). glibc `mallopt` and `mallinfo2` (`net/parallel.rs`, `drive/main.rs`).
- TCP: `net/tcp.rs` has a Linux-only test with `listen`.

### Topics

| Topic | Work | Check before closing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Split the window interface from the Wayland backend. Add the portability gate. | `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes for Windows and macOS. The Linux tests pass. |
| 2 | Add `bare-os`: random bytes, DNS servers, trust roots from the OS store, the local time zone with zone data, counts, allocator tuning. Empty the `known` list of the gate. | Each service has a Linux test. The gate passes with an empty `known` list. |
| 3 | Run on each OS: `bare-drive`, `bare-mcp` and the headless tests on macOS (macbook-pro) and in a Windows VM on archMachine. | The fixture journey and a set of public journeys pass on each OS. |
| 4 | Window backends: Win32 and Cocoa, as planned in decisions.md ("Platforms"). | Open, resize, input and redraw checks on each OS. |

- `bare-window` builds Wayland on Linux only (target dependencies). On other OSes `none.rs` gives the same `Window` and `Waker`. `Window::open` returns "no window backend on windows yet". `Stats` moved to `lib.rs`, because it does not depend on the OS.

## MCP server for end-to-end tests (2026-11-10)

`bare-mcp` is an MCP server over stdio. An agent runs end-to-end tests in `bare` through it. See [decisions.md](decisions.md#mcp-server-for-end-to-end-tests-2026-11-10).

- Tools: `run_steps` (a step file), `open`, `step` and `close` (a live session). The options are `vars`, `secrets_file`, `window`, `width`, `height` and `timeout_ms`. A report is the JSON of `bare-drive`, plus `out`, the folder with the PNGs of `shot` steps and failures. An empty folder is removed at the end of a run.
- A tool error (a bad step, no session) is a result with `isError`. The server then goes on. Unknown methods give -32601, and bad JSON gives -32700.
- Register it: `claude mcp add bare -- <path>/bare-mcp --workspace 6`. Without `--workspace`, a window opens where the compositor puts it.

Checks:

- `crates/mcp/tests/server.rs`, offline, on the fixture app of the driver: the staging step file passes through `run_steps` (27 steps, PNGs written). The same journey passes one line at a time through `open`/`step`/`close`, with unique line numbers. A failed step keeps the session. Bad calls return errors and the server goes on. A run without pictures leaves no folder. No reply holds a secret. 6 passed.
- The `bare-drive` tests pass after the change to `Session`. With `bare-window`: 92 passed, 0 failed.
- Live, archMachine: `run_steps` on example.com (open, click a link, `shot`) and a session on news.ycombinator.com.
- Live, arjun-e16 (Hyprland 0.56.2): `open` with `window: true` and `--workspace 6`. `hyprctl clients` listed `bare`, "bare (driven)", workspace 6. The active workspace stayed 1 before and after. `close` removed the window.
- `tools/portable_check.sh`: scan, Windows and macOS checks pass. `cargo xwin build --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -p bare-mcp` links a PE32+ console executable (12.6 MB).

## Owner decisions: login and E2E scope (2026-11-10)

Goal: `bare` is a minimal browser for logins and end-to-end tests on real sites. It is not shipped as a general browser now.

- Rule: build no feature ahead of need. Fix a gap only when a real login or E2E journey fails on it.
- Approved: session import and export (cookies and storage), so a journey can start from a session made in another browser. This is the answer to bot challenges and 2FA. No challenge bypass. Check before the plan: no such support exists today. `open` in `bare-drive` always starts with a new, empty profile (`crates/drive/src/steps.rs`).
- Closed: draft #345 (`steps-aborts`). The frame diagnostic did not fix the craigslist and apnews budget failures, and its cost stayed above the +0.5% limit. The branch is kept.
- Closed: the glibc-only drift question. No more attribution work.
- Wait for a failing journey: Workers, IndexedDB persistence and cursors, WebAssembly, resizable ArrayBuffer, EventSource, proportional text widths and the layout gaps of module 4.

Not done in this record: the README and decisions.md still state the learning purpose. The owner did not yet decide on a change to them.

## Session state save and load (2026-11-10)

Built: `bare-drive` can save a session to a file and start a new session from it.

- `bare-net`: `Cookie::new` and `Jar::insert` put a stored cookie in the jar. `insert` skips an expired cookie and a public-suffix domain that is not host-only. It does not apply the cookie count limits.
- `bare`: `WebStorage::export` and `import` copy cookies, `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` as plain text (`StorageState`). Import goes through `set`, so the limits hold. A lone UTF-16 surrogate becomes U+FFFD.
- `bare`: `Page::open_in_with`, `Page::reopen_in_with` and `Remote::open_with` start a session from a `StorageState`. The state is plain data, because `WebStorage` is not `Send` and a window runs on its own thread. The old signatures call the new ones with `None`. A restored cookie is sent because the client of a session uses the jar of its storage.
- `bare-drive`: new steps `open URL state="FILE"` and `save-state "FILE"` (`steps.rs`, `state.rs`). The step output gives counts only.
- File format: Playwright `storageState` JSON, plus `sessionStorage` in each origin. A domain with a leading dot is a domain cookie. `expires` is Unix seconds, `-1` for a session cookie. Unknown fields are ignored. The file is written to a temporary file with mode 0600, then renamed. Errors name the file and the field, never a value.
- The 0600 call is in `run.rs` (`private`), because `tools/portable_check.sh` allows OS code only in files on its list.

Checks:
- `cargo test --release -p bare-net --lib cookie`: 22 passed. `-p bare --lib storage`: 13 passed. `-p bare-drive`: all passed (3 new tests in `tests/state.rs`). `-p bare-mcp`: all passed.
- `cargo test --release --workspace`: 3497 passed, 0 failed.
- `tools/portable_check.sh`: passed (scan, Windows, macOS).
- Cost sample: 61 rows (every 13th), base is main 29b4364f00. Glibc mean -0.002%, jemalloc +0.000%. Over the limit under both allocators: 0. Failed: 0.
- The sed expression in the task text for the row filter fails on GNU sed (`[][.` starts a collating symbol). I used `[].[\*^$()+?{}|]`. The base needed `base-build origin/main --release -p bare-stress`.

Not tested: a real Playwright file made in Chrome. The staging login journey. IndexedDB (not saved). A window run (`--window`) of `open ... state=` (the code path exists and compiles; no test runs it). Windows and macOS runs (they only build).

## MCP session cache and ensure_session (2026-11-10)

`bare-mcp` keeps logged-in sessions in memory. New tools: `save_state` (name, optional file) and `ensure_session` (name, url, login, check, optional file). `open` takes `state` (a saved name). `bare-drive` gets `Session::preload` and `Session::export_state`.

Why: an agent needs one call before each test to get a logged-in live page. Cypress `cy.session` validates a restored session and sets it up again when the check fails. We do the same. Memory is the default, so tokens do not touch disk. A reply gives counts only.

## Shot waits for the page to load (2026-11-11, issue #374)

The `open` step only starts the load of the document. The ticks of the next steps finish it. A `shot` right after a live `open` (the `open` and `step` tools) had no tick to wait for, so it saved a blank page. The `shot` step now tries again while `Page::loading()` is true, as it does while pictures load.

Checks: `a_shot_right_after_open_shows_the_loaded_page` in `crates/mcp/tests/server.rs` failed before the fix (17365 bytes, blank) and passes after it. `cargo test -p bare-mcp` passes. `cargo test -p bare-drive` passes except `chunked` (2 tests), which also fails without this change. `survive_limit` is slow (about 45 s) and failed once while other test runs used the CPU. It passes alone.

## CSS translate transform (2026-11-11, issue #376)

Problem: `transform: translateX(-100%)` did nothing. A closed drawer painted over the page.

Built: `transform` and `translate` move a box and all that is inside it. They affect paint, hit tests and all geometry (one move of the fragments, before `fragment::absolute`, next to `position: relative`).

- `bare-css`: two internal properties, `TranslateX` and `TranslateY` (`-bare-translate-x`, `-bare-translate-y`), not in `Property::LISTED`. `transform_declaration` in `values.rs` reads `none`, `translate()`, `translateX()`, `translateY()`, `translate3d()` (z is dropped) and the `translate` property. Values: `px` and the other lengths, `%`, `calc()`, `0`. `inherit`, `initial` and `unset` work. Several translations add up when the units agree; a mix is not good (the declaration is dropped).
- `bare-layout` (`lib.rs`): each box that is not a non-atomic inline box moves by the values. A percent is of the border box of the box. Other boxes are not laid out again.
- Other transform functions (`rotate`, `scale`, `skew`, `matrix`, `perspective`) are good values that do nothing.

Gaps: no rotate, scale, skew or matrix. `transform` and `translate` together: the later declaration wins (the spec combines them). A transform does not make a stacking context or a containing block for `fixed` and `absolute` boxes. `transform-origin` is not read. The scrollable area does not count the moved box. `getComputedStyle(el).transform` is still `undefined`. An inline box that is not atomic does not move. `translate: calc(1px + 2px) 3px` (spaces inside `calc`) is not good. No `var()` check beyond the shared path.

Checks (release): `cargo test --workspace`: 3506 passed, 0 failed. New tests: `values::tests::transform_translate`, `block::tests::translate_moves_a_box_and_what_is_inside`, `hit::tests::a_translated_box_is_hit_where_it_is_drawn`, `paint::translate_moves_what_is_painted`. `tools/portable_check.sh`: ok. The page of the issue, painted with `bare --paint`, shows no red.

Not tested: `bare-mcp` and a window on the page of the issue. Animation of `transform`. A real drawer site.

## EventSource (#375, 2026-11-11)

`EventSource` now exists, and it delivers each event as it arrives. It is a JavaScript shim (`crates/bare/src/shims/eventsource.js`) on top of `XMLHttpRequest`, made at the first read of the name like `Path2D` (`browser_shims.rs`). `Heap::browser_name` in `crates/js/src/heap.rs` lists the name.

What it does: a GET with `Accept: text/event-stream` and `Last-Event-ID`; `open`, `message` and named events; `lastEventId`, `retry`, comments, a BOM, `\r\n`, `\n` and `\r` line ends (also split over two chunks); an unended last event is dropped; `close()`; `withCredentials`; `readyState` and its constants. When the stream ends, it fires `error` with state 0 and connects again after the retry time (3000 ms by default). A status other than 200, or a type other than `text/event-stream`, fires `error` and closes (a 502, 503 or 504 reconnects, as does a network error).

Live streaming (see "Event streams outside the fetch queue" in decisions.md): an XHR GET that asks for `text/event-stream` is not in the queue of `fetch`. Its own thread reads the body and sends each chunk to the page. The loader loop delivers the chunks (`Browser::run_streams`), and the XHR fires `readystatechange` and `progress` in state 3 for each one. A later `fetch` or XHR does not wait for the stream. Caps: 6 open streams on a page, 1 MiB of body on a stream (then a network error and a reconnect).

Gaps:
- Events are `Event` objects with `data`, `origin`, `lastEventId`, `source` and `ports`. `MessageEvent` is not a constructor here, so `e instanceof MessageEvent` is false.
- A closed stream ends its thread at the next chunk or at the read timeout of the connection (30 s), not at once.
- A server that sends nothing for 30 s ends the stream with a read timeout. `EventSource` then connects again.
- Only an XHR that asks for `text/event-stream` streams. Other XHR replies and all `fetch` bodies still arrive whole.

Checks: `cargo test -p bare --lib eventsource`: 9 passed. New tests: `events_arrive_while_the_stream_is_open`, `an_event_split_over_chunks_fires_once`, `close_stops_the_events`, `a_post_completes_while_a_stream_is_open`, and in `crates/mcp/tests/server.rs` `an_open_event_stream_delivers_events_and_does_not_block_a_fetch`. All failed before the change; the MCP test failed with `no element matches text="fetch done"`. `cargo test -p bare`: 1291 passed, 2 failed (`browser_canvas_tests::one_image_data_holds_at_most_64_mib` fails on main too; `browser_session_tests::a_pending_meta_refresh_is_queued_work` is flaky and passed alone). `cargo test -p bare-mcp -p bare-drive`: all pass except `chunked` (2 tests), which fails on main too. `cargo clippy`: no warning on a changed line. `tools/portable_check.sh`: ok. The app `deck` in `bare-mcp`: a new chat sends its message, the run streams, and the screenshot shows in the chat.

Not tested: `withCredentials` with cookies. A cross-origin stream (CORS). HTTP/2 streams. Chrome comparison of the event order.

## Benchmark round on frozen commits (2026-11-13)

The owner asked for a benchmark of everything built so far. Main stays open, because other agents keep merging into it. We measure two frozen commits. A fix is rebased on the newest main and measured again there before merge.

- BASE: `13c6b0bc` (merge of #365, status at the pause, 2026-11-10).
- NEW: `f6415364` (merge of #456, 2026-11-13).

Three agents ran at the same time on archMachine. Instruction counts do not depend on load. Wall times do, so all time numbers below are weak. Raw logs and reports are machine-local under `/data/bare-tmp/bm/{a,b,c}/`. `/usr/bin/time` is not installed, so max RSS comes from `wait4` or `getrusage`. `/data/bare-tmp/bin` (`heavy`, `base-build`) was missing on archMachine and was restored from arjun-e16 with archMachine paths and 3 slots. `merge-gate` is missing on both machines.

### A: cost matrix, bench and stress

- Cost matrix (813 rows): 171 rows over +0.5% under both allocators, 30 under one allocator only. Mean glibc change +0.640%, median +0.084%. Worst rows: `focus_load` +9.1%, `nodelist_load` +7.5%, `boxes-display-none` +6.9%. The largest decrease is -1.45%.
- `parse_load deep 1` and `deep 10` overflow the stack in NEW. d88ad8ac raised `HARD_MAX_DEPTH` from 256 to 2048, and `crates/js/examples/parse_load.rs` still runs on a 2 MiB thread. The example is stale; the parser is not slower.
- Bench: memory is the same in every step except `css: styles of 200,000 elements` (peak +6.5%, kept +10.3%).
- Stress: no case has a growth exponent over 1.5 in either tree. Memory at 100x grew in `css-is-wide` (+79.7%), `css-var-many` (+35.5%), `css-var-cycle` (+20.0%), `css-var-fanout` (+17.1%) and `css-unique-styles` (+11.7%). `css-class-index` at 2,000,000 timed out in BASE and finishes in NEW (7.8 s).
- Hypothesis: ff3cd703 "Keep custom property sets as numbers" caused the css-var memory growth. Not verified.

### B: ramps up to the raised limits

| Limit | NEW passes up to | BASE refused at | Worst passing point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Task steps (500M) | 55M loop iterations | 12M | 9 to 10 s, 15 MiB |
| Computed work, simple page | 32k nodes, 32k rules | 12k | 152 ms, 56 MiB |
| Computed work, 6 classes and descendant rules | N=22000 | 16000 | 1.16 s, 71 MiB |
| Whole-page restyles (6000 elements, 36000 rules) | 13 restyles | 2 | about 1 s |
| Style sheet, external | 16 MiB (then `css-resource-bytes`) | 4 MiB (`cssom-text`) | 2.1 s, 970 MiB |
| Nested calls | 1022 deep (then traversal depth) | 200 | 20 ms, 15 MiB |

- Every limit refuses cleanly, and growth is linear except the heavy computed-work page (instruction exponent 1.4 to 2.0).
- A loop iteration costs about 9 steps. One step costs about 19 ns.
- A restyle is charged about 35M steps but takes about 65 ms. The charge is about 10 times too high.
- The 32 MiB sheet cap is never reached: the 8 MiB body cap and the 16 MiB resource cap refuse first. `cssom-objects` stops a page that reads `cssRules` of a dense 1 MiB sheet or a realistic 4 MiB sheet.

### C: whole-browser journeys

All 48 public journeys ran 3 times on each commit, alternating, and headless Chrome ran 3 times on each URL.

- Totals over 48 journeys (min of passing runs): instructions 23,978 M to 24,945 M (+4.0%). Min wall 49,349 ms to 48,945 ms (-0.8%). RSS 1,172 MiB to 1,182 MiB (+0.9%). Median RSS 16.4 MiB to 17.5 MiB.
- All 48 pass at least once on both commits. `nextjs-docs` and `duckduckgo-html-search` are flaky on both.
- Live pages vary up to +124% in instructions between runs of the same binary. Flags on `react-docs`, `paulgraham-home`, `curl-se-home` and `python-org-docs-link` are noise.
- Over +5% instructions: 13 journeys, for example `rust-book-search` +15%, `wikipedia-search` +14%, `mdn-reference` +11.5%. Over +10% RSS: `wikipedia-article`, `wikipedia-search`, `wikipedia-toc-languages`.
- Heaviest in NEW: `rust-book-search` (4.46 G instructions, 96 MiB) and `python-docs-search-results` (2.74 G, 100 MiB).
- Chrome: median load 528 ms and median RSS 1,216 MiB summed over its processes. Chrome time covers the first navigation only, and bare time covers the whole journey.

### Fix candidates, in order

1. Restyle step charge (about 10 times too high): pages run out of budget early.
2. Heavy computed-work page: exponent 1.4 to 2.0.
3. CSS memory: `css-is-wide` and the `css-var-*` cases.
4. Top cost matrix rows: `focus_load`, `nodelist_load`, `boxes-display-none`.
5. `parse_load.rs` stack size for the 2048 depth.
6. A 16 MiB external sheet at 970 MiB RSS.

Not tested: wall time on an idle machine, stress `fuzz`, Gmail and other logged-in pages, and layout and paint cost on the ramps. `bare-drive` is stripped, so perf could not name hot functions.

## Profiles, designs and the performance goal (2026-11-13)

Two profiles ran on the frozen commit `f6415364` with a symbol build. Reports are machine-local under `/data/bare-tmp/prof/{cpu,mem}/`.

- CPU share on the 48 journeys (frame-pointer stacks, 144 runs): JS execution 25.5%, style 17.7%, sheet loader 10.7%, CSS parse 8.9%, layout 6.9%, JS parse 6.6%. On the ramps: JS execution 57.7%, style 32.2%.
- `Run::tell_links` walks the whole DOM for each sheet that loads: O(sheets x nodes). It reaches 30.5% of `python-org-docs-link`.
- Memory: the median journey peaks at 18.2 MiB, and 77% of it is the program image. The heaviest journey (`python-docs-search-results`, 116 MiB) is 39% JS heap, 19% script ASTs and 18% DOM. `wrap_declaration` copies about 130 accessors onto each CSSOM rule object: 10.2 KB per rule, 671 MiB at the cap of 65,536 objects.

Design documents: `docs/design-style.md`, `docs/design-js.md`, and an independent review in `docs/design-review.md`. Main findings: 95% of parsed JS syntax nodes are in functions that never run, about 13% of CSS rule entries ever match, and the sheet scans visit 110 times more nodes than the cascade styles.
