- `test262_check.sh` and `exec_diff.sh` not run: no change in `crates/js`.

### Not tested

- Real network timing. `diverged` assumes that a page of the same site makes the same lists in the same order. With a real network the lists of the first look can differ, and then an idle set goes one document early (a lost gain, never a wrong style). The corpus replay uses a virtual clock.
- A page with many frames (each frame is a document of the thread: its look counts for `diverged` and `new_document`). A suite on more than one worker. The wall time of the suite and of the journeys (shared machine). The 800-test suite has 1 run. The 15-run RSS rows use the build with the experiment switches (same code path as the final build; the final build was measured with 9 runs).
- `heap_bytes` is read once for each set when it is first idle. The set grows by 3% after that (`python-org-docs-link`).
- The measurement counters, the switches and the synthetic stream are not in the repository: `/data/bare-tmp/rcb/` (`experiment-all.patch`, `an.py`, `peaks.py`, `sim.py`, the traces in `trace/`).

### Noticed, not changed

- RSS of one journey moves by 2% to 3% from run to run on the same binary; the sum by 0.3%. A change of 1% on the Wikipedia rows needs 9 or more runs to show.
- `Counts.rules` (rules in the cache) is removed with `MAX_RULES`; nothing used it.


## Modern color rendering, 2026-11-14

Issue #464. Candidate production source: 79164130. Modern absolute colors and two-operand mixes now reach the existing sRGB painter. Deferred currentColor expressions share the variable arena. Color stays four bytes, Value eight bytes and Side 72 bytes. Stored deferred entries grow from 32 to 56 bytes. The color crate uses its Rust libm backend to avoid an extra shared-library load on ordinary pages.

The final serial release run passes 1,913 tests with seven ignored. The selected three-row browser cost gate passes its unchanged 0.5 percent rule under both allocators. The final 390-pixel synthetic page and real Deck primary button pass computed-color and inspected-pixel checks. The tests use headless bare; no mirrored test is claimed. Full resource samples, failed intermediate checks and syntax limits are in [the results](rendering-colors-results.md).

No installation, merge or deployment is included. Wrapping remains separate in #467.


## 2026-11-14: grapheme-safe wrapping

Source 6841f650 adds inherited wrap properties and shared grapheme opportunities for placement and intrinsic sizing. The serial release checks pass 1,917 tests. The five selected cost rows pass under both allocators. Computed style grows by 16 bytes. Phone-width captures show the same request text wrapping inside the Deck card. The diagnostic rerun and all test limits are in [the results](rendering-wrap-results.md). No installation or merge is included.
## Final benchmark of the perf goal (2026-11-14)

Task: measure the 8 success criteria of `docs/perf-goal.md` on two frozen commits. No code changed. Raw logs and TSV files are machine-local under `/data/bare-tmp/fb/`.

- BASE: `f6415364`, the baseline of the goal. NEW: `8f23dded`, main after every step merged (#519).
- Machine: archMachine (AMD Ryzen 9 5900HX, 16 cores, 30 GiB). The machine was shared: load average 2.5 to 10 during the runs, and up to 3 other `heavy` jobs. Instruction counts are stable under load (spread 0.3% or less on every journey). Wall times are weak.
- Build: all three `bare-drive` binaries come from `cargo build --release -p bare-drive` (a `--workspace --examples` build does not make the `bare-drive` binary, and an earlier agent saw a 2.5% difference between the two build kinds). NEW and BASE: `base-build <sha> --release -p bare-drive`. The cost matrix and the stress runs use the `base-build` default trees (`--release --workspace --examples`) plus `--release -p bare-stress`.
- BASE for the journeys is the baseline with the replay patch and the virtual clock: local branch `bench-base-vclock` in `/data/bare-tmp/bench-base-src` (HEAD `2ddee1da` plus the staged clock patch, not pushed). It is `f6415364` plus `crates/net` replay, seed, and clock code. For the ramps, the suite, the stress cases and the cost matrix BASE is `f6415364` itself (no patch).
- Corpus: `/data/bare-tmp/corpus/virtual`, 47 journeys, virtual clock (`journeys.sh compare --clock virtual --runs 3 --pss`). The runner makes run 0 (PSS) and runs 1 to 3. Medians below are over runs 1 to 3.

### Criterion 1 and 2: the journeys

Inputs: corpus `virtual`, 47 journeys, 3 runs plus the PSS run for each journey and binary (94 journey-binaries, 4 runs each, runs interleaved). Command: `tools/bench/journeys.sh compare --clock virtual --runs 3 --pss /data/bare-tmp/fb/bin/bare-drive-base-vclock /data/bare-tmp/fb/bin/bare-drive-new`. Log: `/data/bare-tmp/fb/journeys.{log,tsv}`.

- All 47 journeys pass in all runs on both binaries. The same-binary spread of instructions is 0.3% or less on every journey (target of the clock task: under 2%). The replay has zero misses, except `mdn-reference` on NEW (47 misses in each of its 4 runs) and 1 miss in run 0 of `wikipedia-toc-languages` on BASE.
- **`mdn-reference` on NEW does not do the recorded work.** It asks for 47 JS chunk files at a wrong address (`GET https://developer.mozilla.org:443/en-US/7489.879b548e785958fd.js`, and 46 more like it; the recording has them under another path) and no reply is recorded for them. The journey still passes. Its instructions fall from 6,978 M to 1,862 M (-73.3%) and its peak RSS from 116.0 MiB to 29.6 MiB. That is not a gain. I ran the journey with `BARE_NET_REPLAY` on the merge commits in between: 0 misses at `226935a5` and `0727ffef` (#498), 47 misses from `e497ff5f` (#492) up to NEW. So PR #492 changed the address of these requests. Hypothesis: the page builds the chunk address from a script address or a script property (a webpack public path), and the lazy function parse of #492 changes that value. Not examined. On the live site this would be 47 failed chunk loads. This looks like a correctness regression; it needs an issue and a fix. I did not change code.
- Without `mdn-reference`, the 46 other journeys give: instructions 98,211 M to 87,857 M (ratio 0.895), CPU 11,220 ms to 10,389 ms (0.926), peak RSS 1,989.7 MiB to 1,712.0 MiB (0.860). I report 85.3% (all 47, as measured) and 89.5% (without it). Both miss the 80% target.
- Totals, sum of medians: instructions 105,189 M to 89,719 M (-14.7%, ratio 0.853). CPU (user+system) 12,090 ms to 10,579 ms (-12.5%). Wall 11,343 ms to 10,190 ms (-10.2%, loaded machine). Peak RSS 2,105.7 MiB to 1,741.6 MiB (-17.3%).

- Median change of a journey: -13.7%. Geometric mean of the ratios: 0.729. 36 journeys are more than 5% lower, 9 are within 5%, 2 are more than 5% higher (`wiktionary-portal` +10.6%, `paulgraham-home` +10.3%).
- The total is held up by five journeys: `react-docs` (16,936 M), `rust-book-search` (16,315 M), `wikipedia-article` (7,701 M), `wikipedia-search` (7,244 M) and `nodejs-org-home` (5,864 M). They are 60.3% of the NEW total, and they moved by -0.8% (54,510 M to 54,060 M). The other 42 journeys went from 50,679 M to 35,659 M (70.4%). Hypothesis: these five spend their instructions in page JS execution, which the steps of the goal did not reduce much (the profile of 2026-11-13 gave JS execution 25.5% of the journeys and 57.7% of the ramps). Not measured per subsystem on NEW.

### Criterion 8: the limits

- Restyle charge. Method: a page that restyles 6,002 elements (the `rest_13` page with 3,000 loops, element count from the step 4 notes) runs until the 500 M step budget of a task ends the script (`LIVE_TASK_STEPS`, `crates/bare/src/page.rs`). Then instructions divided by the budget is the instruction cost of one charged step. `/data/bare-tmp/fb/pages/rest_3000_j.html` logs the loop counter every 25 loops.
  - BASE: the budget ends after 14 or fewer restyles (the ramps: `rest_13` passes, `rest_15` stops) at 11,636 M instructions: 23 instructions for each charged step.
  - NEW: the budget ends after 1,700 to 1,724 restyles at 102,842 M instructions (60.1 M for each restyle): 206 instructions for each charged step.
  - A step of a plain JS loop costs 198 instructions (`steps_5000000` to `steps_50000000`: 1,805 instructions for each iteration, about 9.1 steps for each iteration, from the benchmark round of 2026-11-13, section B: 55 M iterations fit in 500 M steps).
  - So the charge was about 9 times the cost on BASE (23 against about 200) and is 1.04 times the cost on NEW (206 against 198). Met. `STEPS_PER_RESTYLED_ELEMENT` is 32 (`crates/bare/src/browser_computed.rs:229`). One run each, deterministic.
- `cssom-objects` cap. `MAX_OBJECTS = 1 << 19` (524,288) at `crates/bare/src/browser_cssom.rs:20`, and `MAX_RULES = 1 << 21`. The old value was 65,536. The cap is not removed and is not computed from the rule count: it is a fixed constant chosen from the measured bytes of a read rule (585 B, about 290 MiB at the cap). Probes in criterion 5: the realistic 16 MiB sheet (187,852 rules) is read in full, and the dense one (844,366 rules) stops at the cap. A different limit, `style-objects` (65,536), binds first when a page reads `.style` of every rule. Not met as written ("removed or set by the rule count"). It is met in effect for the biggest sheet the loader accepts that has realistic rules. I report it as partly met.
- The `computed-work` cap is unchanged (nodes times rules). The step 4 section shows it refuses `comp_48000` and `compm_34000`, which cost 1 to 3 G with the index. I did not re-measure that.

`bare-stress scale css` (50 style cases, each at 1x, 10x and 100x of its base size, one process for each size), BASE and NEW `bare-stress`, 3 runs each, alternating. The exponent is `log(time at the last size / time at 1x) / log(size ratio)` from wall time inside the process (not instructions: this tool measures time). - Memory (peak MB of the counting allocator at the largest size that ran, median of 3 runs). 41 cases have a peak of 5 MB or more on one tree. 19 of them are within 5%. ### What was not tested

- Wall time on an idle machine. Load average was 2.5 to 10, and wall numbers are in the tables as weak.
- The live sites. The journeys replay a recorded corpus on a virtual clock. The 48th journey, `nextjs-docs`, does not pass on replay (an engine stop at `checkVisibility`, section "Repeatable journey benchmark"). I did not run it live and did not re-check it.
- The corpus `virtual` was recorded by older binaries. NEW asks for different requests on `mdn-reference` (47 misses). A recording by NEW could change the totals of that journey and of any other that differs without a miss.
- A real login or a real network in the suite (the fixture login is cheap). The suite with `--login-ms`. The `run_suite` tool of `bare-mcp`. A suite of more than 40 tests.
- Window mode, Windows and macOS. A second machine.
- The BASE tree through the test262 gate: only the baseline file was compared. The cost matrix and `bare-stress` ran on `--workspace --examples` builds, and the journeys and ramps on `-p bare-drive` builds, so a few instruction counts do not compare across them.
- The cause of any regression above (#492 on `wiktionary-portal`, `wikipedia-portal` and `mdn-reference`; #506 on `paulgraham-home`; #497, #512 and #515 on RSS of `python-docs-search-results`). I named the PR that introduced each one by running binaries of the merge commits. The reasons are hypotheses.
- BASE for the journeys is the local, unpushed branch `bench-base-vclock`. The result depends on that patch (replay, seed and clock only).
- PSS: the sampler of run 0 missed 17 of 47 journeys. The PSS figures are not a criterion and are partial.
- Probes on `style-objects` and the dense sheet are 1 run each.

### Noticed, not changed

- PR #492 changes the requests of `mdn-reference`: 47 chunk files are asked for at `/en-US/<chunk>.js`. It needs an issue and a fix. A journey that passes with misses hides this (the runner prints the misses, but a pass is still a pass). A gate on `misses == 0` in `journeys.sh compare` would catch it.
- `wiktionary-portal` +10.6%, `wikipedia-portal` +4.2% (PR #492) and `paulgraham-home` +10.3% (PR #506) cost more instructions than BASE.
- The five heaviest journeys (60% of the instructions) did not move (-0.8%). The next gain for criterion 2 is in page JS execution, not in style, layout or parse.
- Criterion 6 was met at #501 and lost by 6 to 9 MiB since. A bound on the memory of #497, #512 and #515 would bring it back.
- The PSS sampler of `journeys.sh` misses short journeys. Hypothesis: a journey shorter than about 100 ms ends before the sampler (every 20 ms, after the `perf` child starts) sees the process. Not checked.
- The step budget gives 206 instructions for each charged step on a restyle loop and 198 on a JS loop. They agree within 5%, so the 32 steps for each restyled element hold today.

## Fix: `import()` and `import.meta` in a lazy function belong to its module (2026-11-14)

Branch `t3/fix-lazy-js-chunk-path`, on `8f879534`. Fixes the regression that the final benchmark found in `mdn-reference` (PR #492, lazy function bodies).

### Cause

`mdn-reference` loads a bundler runtime, `/static/client/runtime.<hash>.js`, an ES module of 19,664 bytes. Its loader is `import("./" + o.u(chunk))`, in a function of the runtime. A browser resolves `./<chunk>.js` against the module's address, `/static/client/`. Since #492 the function is lazy: its first call parses it again and runs the tree in a script slot of its own (`lazy_load`). `mod_of_current` found the module by comparing the running script slot with the slot of each module. The slot of a lazy tree is no module's slot, so `import()` gave no referrer, the host resolved against the page (`/en-US/`), and `import.meta` in such a function threw "import.meta outside a module". Verified: the recorded runtime has `o.p="/static/client/"` and `import("./"+o.u(s))`, and the replay asked for `/en-US/7489.879b548e785958fd.js`; the chunks are recorded under `/static/client/`. Hypotheses in the benchmark (`document.currentScript`, stack file names, a regex) were not the cause.

### Change

- `Interp.lazy_owner` (`eval.rs`): the slot of each lazy tree, mapped to the slot of the script that holds its stub. Filled in `lazy_load` (`eval_scripts.rs`), after the tree is walked.
- `mod_of_current` (`eval_modules.rs`) follows `lazy_owner` up to the slot that a module owns (a lazy function inside a lazy tree takes more than one step). It runs only for `import()` and `import.meta`. Lazy parsing stays on for modules and pages.
- Other readers of the current script slot do not need it: `hscope_find` reads handler functions, which are small and never lazy. The stack frames key by slot and keep working.

### Tests (written first, failing on main)

- `eval_modules_tests::a_dropped_function_of_a_module_is_still_code_of_that_module`: a module of 20 KB with two lazy functions (one nested in a lazy function) that call `import()` and read `import.meta.url`. Failed with `Unsupported("import.meta outside a module")`, passes now.
- `browser_loader_tests::a_dynamic_import_in_a_lazy_function_is_relative_to_its_module`: a page loads `/static/rt.js` (long, lazy `load(n)` with `import('./' + n + '.js')`); the chunk must come from `/static/c1.js`. Fails on main (empty log), passes now.
- No `exec_diff` case: the byte lane refuses module syntax (`bc_gen_expr.rs`), so the fixtures hold no module code.

### `journeys.sh compare` checks replay misses

`compare` prints "Replay misses" at the end: per journey, the most misses of runs 1 to N for each binary. A journey fails when NEW has more than BASE; the script prints `FAILED` and exits 1. A miss that BASE also has (the `wikipedia-portal` beacon POST, 1 each) does not fail. Run 0 (PSS) is left out, because its timing gives misses that the other runs do not. `run` prints the most misses of a journey after its median line. Check: `compare` of `0727ffef` against `e497ff5f` on `mdn-reference` prints `base 0 new 47 FAILED` (exit 1); a unit check of the report on made-up rows (mdn 0 vs 47, wp 1 vs 1, run-0 only miss) fails only the first.

### Numbers (archMachine, corpus `virtual`, `BARE_CLOCK=virtual`, `bare-drive` built with `-p bare-drive`, instructions are the median of 3 runs)

`mdn-reference` replay: 47 misses on main (`8f879534`), 0 on this branch (1 run, then 3 runs of the full set below). Instructions: 2,102.3 M on main, 7,179.3 M on this branch (+241.5%), peak RSS 31.9 to 113.9 MiB. This rise is expected: the page code now runs. The merge before #492 (`0727ffef`) gave 6,978 M and 116.0 MiB in the benchmark. The branch is +2.9% above that. Hypothesis: later merges changed the cost of the page's code; not examined.

The 47 journeys, main against branch, 3 runs: all pass, same-binary spread 0.4% or less on the branch (2.3% on main for `wikipedia-toc-languages`, 1 run with 1 miss). Except `mdn-reference`, no journey moves by more than 0.1% in instructions. Total 90,359 M to 95,445 M (+5.6%, all from `mdn-reference`; 88,257 M to 88,266 M without it). Peak RSS sums: 1,694 to 1,775 MiB (`mdn-reference` +82 MiB; others within noise, `wikipedia-article` +2.5 MiB with equal instructions). Misses: `mdn-reference` 47 to 0, `wikipedia-toc-languages` 1 to 0. The total of the final benchmark (85.3%) changes with this fix: its `mdn-reference` row was 1,862 M instead of about 7,100 M.

### `wiktionary-portal` and `wikipedia-portal`: not the same cause

Instructions, M, median of 3 runs, 0 misses in all runs, spread 0.1% or less:

| Journey | `0727ffef` (before #492) | `e497ff5f` (#492) | main `8f879534` | this branch |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `wiktionary-portal` | 1,213.4 | 1,582.5 | 1,559.9 | 1,560.0 |
| `wikipedia-portal` | 999.9 | 1,254.4 | 1,233.0 | 1,233.0 |

The fix gives no change on either. They have no module with `import()`; the cost step is still #492. Hypothesis (not measured): the second parse and the extra script slot of the lazy functions that these pages call. They have a standing exception in "Standing exception: PR #492" for another row only; these two rows need their own look (a source-size threshold for lazy bodies, or cheaper second parse).

### Checks

- `cargo test --release --workspace --no-fail-fast`: all pass except the 7 TLS tests that fail on main (`https_openssl` 2, `client_openssl` 4, `tls12_openssl` 1) and `a_hidden_iframe_download_is_saved` (flaky under load; passes alone).
- `tools/js/cost_matrix.sh` against main `8f879534`: 803 rows, 0 rows over under both allocators, 0 over under glibc, mean +0.000%; `parse_load deep 1` and `deep 10` do not run (known stack overflow).
- `TEST262=/data/claude-tmp/test262 tools/js/test262_check.sh`: exit 0, no directory below the baseline.
- `tools/js/exec_diff.sh`: 79 runs, 0 differences.
- `tools/js/typing/keycost.sh`: 295.6 M for each key (`#a1`), 301.0 M (`#f0`), load and mount 613.7 M, peak RSS 30.9 and 31.0 MiB. Not compared with main (no change on the typing path; the cost matrix has the rows).

### Not tested

A live run on developer.mozilla.org (the chunks load on the recorded corpus only). `import()` inside a lazy function of a classic script (no referrer there, as before). A realm shared across threads with `lazy_owner` (the map is per realm, as `lazy`). Windows and macOS.

### Noticed, not changed

- `wiktionary-portal` and `wikipedia-portal` still cost 28% and 23% more than before #492 (above).
- A page that passes with replay misses stayed unseen for a whole benchmark round; `journeys.sh run` still shows misses only as a count, and other tools (`run_suite`) have no such check.

## Correction of criterion 2 after PR #521 (2026-11-14)

The final benchmark gave 85.3% for criterion 2. That total held a broken `mdn-reference` row: the journey did not load its chunk files. ## R2-D: why lazy JS functions cost more on the portal journeys (2026-11-14)

Task: measure and design, docs only. Design: `docs/design-js-reparse.md`. Main `28a8fbc2`. Counters and scripts: `/data/bare-tmp/r2/R2-D/` (`counters.patch`, `r2d.rs`, `sweep*.sh`, `s1` to `s4` raw rows). Machine archMachine, corpus `virtual`, 3 runs per journey and mode (counter files: 1 run).

### Result

- **The hypothesis holds, with a correction.** The first parse of a long function is a full parse that drops its nodes, not a preparse. A function that runs is parsed again, and so is every long function inside it. A function `d` lazy functions deep that runs is parsed `d + 2` times. Depth reaches 7.
- `wiktionary-portal`: 1,561 M lazy, 1,239 M with lazy functions off (same binary), 1,213 M before #492. Second parses 331.4 M (655 functions, 3.04 MB), load step 19.9 M, walk saved -39.1 M. `wikipedia-portal`: 1,234 M, 996 M, 1,000 M. Second parses 237.8 M (703, 2.11 MB), load 16.0 M, walk saved -25.6 M.
- 47 journeys: lazy 95,488 M, lazy off 91,998 M (+3,490 M, +3.8%), `nonest` (lazy only in the first tree) 93,804 M. Peak RSS sums 1,779.7 / 1,841.6 / 1,800.3 MiB. Split of the 3,490 M: second parses +3,115.5 M, load +357.6 M, walk saved -809.0 M, slot swaps +822.5 M.
- **A second cause: slot swaps.** Each lazy function is a script slot. A call across slots swaps 11 interpreter fields, about 190 instructions. `react-docs` has 1.40 M more swaps than eager code (272 M), `nodejs-org-home` 0.67 M (129 M), `github-docs-home` 0.44 M (83 M). This explains the rows that the second parses do not.
- Not the cause: the parse cache (0 hits on the portals), the regex compile (185 programs, 42 M, lazy is cheaper than the old walk-time compile), the garbage collector.
- Share of lazy functions that run: depth 0, 37% by count and 75% by bytes (3,470 of 9,471; 13.91 of 18.44 MB). The portals: 85% and 83%. 66% of the second-parse bytes are lazy bodies inside the function (17.34 of 26.37 MB).
- Raising `LAZY_MIN_BODY` from 128 to 8,192 gives -1.6% instructions and +5.3% RSS on 18 journeys. It is a weak lever.

### Recommendation

A: keep skip data (end position, strictness, inner table) for lazy functions inside a lazy function, as V8 skippable functions and the JSC `SourceProviderCache` do. Estimate: -1,989 M over the 47 journeys (range 1.6 to 2.4 G), `wiktionary-portal` about 1,317 M, `wikipedia-portal` about 1,072 M, RSS unchanged (0.3% for the table). Then S: make a slot swap one pointer swap (estimate -730 M). Criterion 2: 90.1% to about 88.2% (A) and 87.5% (A and S). Not B1 (no lazy functions: -3,490 M, but +61.9 MiB RSS), B2 (a higher body limit), B3 (a heuristic), or C (a record of which functions ran: no gain on a cold run). Fallback: D, measured -1,685 M, +20.6 MiB.

### Not tested

A prototype of A or S (their gain is arithmetic from counters and swap counts; the per-byte cost of inner bodies may differ by 20%). Swap counts on 39 of the 47 journeys. RSS of A. Live sites, other platforms, the byte lane. The cause of +25 M at lazy off against `0727ffef` on `wiktionary-portal` (23 merges in between).

### Noticed, not changed

- Data literals only exist in the lazy parse mode (`self.lazy`). A switch that turns lazy parsing off also turns them off. A first sweep of this task did that and gave a false -857 M on `python-docs-search`.
- `journeys.sh`-style runs under heavy load showed 1 to 4 replay misses on four `wikipedia-*` rows of the threshold sweep. The main sweeps had 0.
- The parse cache keeps one entry for the lazy kind and one for the eager kind of the same text (from #492).

## R2-B: where the Wikipedia journeys spend instructions (2026-11-14, docs only)

Design: `docs/design-wikipedia-journeys.md`. Task R2-B of the round 2 plan. No product code changed. Machine-local files: `/data/bare-tmp/r2/R2-B/` (counter patch, no-settle patch, profiles, TSV files).

Method: symbol build of main `28a8fbc2`; `perf record -e instructions:u -c 500000` with frame pointers, 3 runs per journey; counters in a patch (`BARE_FORCE_STATS`); the corpus `virtual`. Instruction spread of the journeys: 0.1% (`wikipedia-article`, 3 runs: 7,776 M), 0.0 to 3.1% (`wikipedia-search`, 7,338 M; run 0 had 2 timing misses).

Measured split (mean of 3 profile runs, spread 0.5 points or less):

| Subsystem | `wikipedia-article` | `wikipedia-search` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Style | 30.7% | 25.2% |
| JS execution | 22.5% | 22.3% |
| Window named-property list rebuilt (`browser_frames::build`) | 11.5% | 10.7% |
| Layout | 8.8% | 11.9% |
| JS parse | 8.4% | 10.6% |
| Other (DOM bindings 3.7%, selector API 2.7%, HTML 2.4%, CSS parse 2.3%, regexp 1.8%, rest) | 18.1% | 18.7% |

Findings:

- The round 1 hypothesis (the heavy journeys are bound by page JS) is wrong for Wikipedia. JS is 33% and 35%. Style, layout and the name list are 51% and 48%.
- The replay driver's `settle_pictures` loop is 74% of `wikipedia-article`, 56% of `wikipedia-search` and 52.8% of all 47 journeys (95,376 M with it, 45,037 M without; all journeys pass without it). The baseline pays it too: criterion 2 is 90.7% with it and 89.3% without it (2 runs each, `-p bare-drive` builds). `react-docs` is 99.3% loop (16,948 M to 127 M). Owner decision needed: keep or bound the loop (both sides, baseline measured again).
- Window names: 54 and 40 rebuilds of a list of every id of the page (15 k nodes, 17 M each) for 16 and 18 global names that do not exist. All stale by `name_revision`. 894 M and 785 M.
- Style: 8 full passes (782 M) for one load of the long article, caused by 4 appended sheets, 2 restyles that gave up and 2 frame requests. One hover restyled 90,232 elements (9 times the document, 865 M, 10.8% of the article): covered roots are styled again. The 10 "kept" layouts of each journey reused 0 fragments.
- Memory (`massif`, one run): heap peak 50.6 MB, of which JS objects 27.6%, JS trees 10.5%, DOM attributes 7%, layout fragments 8%. RSS without the loop: 33.0 MiB against 60.3 MiB.

Recommendation: W1 (window name by one walk, no list), H1 (skip a covered restyle root), S-A (one retained cascade and layout updated by damage marks). Estimate on the settled benchmark: article -38.5%, search -32.8%, the two -5.4 G (5.7% of the total): criterion 2 from 90.7% to about 85.5%. If the four other Wikipedia journeys gain 25 to 35% (hypothesis), 82 to 83%. The arithmetic is in section 7 of the design.

Not measured: the four other Wikipedia journeys; the roots of the 90 k restyle (cause is a hypothesis); why a reload of the same page pays the same rule-build cost; wall time; the live sites.

## Style round 2: measurements and design (R2-E, 2026-11-14)

Task R2-E of the round 2 plan. Design: [design-style-round2.md](design-style-round2.md). Docs only. Base: main `28a8fbc2`. Machine: archMachine. Each case ran 3 times. The spread of instruction counts was 0.

### Criterion 3: what is left in `compm_22000` and `rest_13`

Driver totals: `compm_22000` 1,835 M (target 1,166 M, -36.5%), `rest_13` 1,240 M (target 1,087 M, -12.3%).

| Stage (M instructions) | `compm_22000` | `rest_13` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| HTML parse | 131 (7.1%) | 25 (2.0%) |
| Rule set build | 130 (7.1%) | 210 (16.9%) |
| First full compute | 581 (31.7%) | 103 (8.3%) |
| Restyles (2 and 13) | 825 (45.0%) | 456 (36.8%) |
| JS, layout, glue, exit | 169 (9.2%) | 450 (36.3%) |

- PR #494 and #502 facts: one build per ramp (confirmed). Build share 7.1% and 16.9% (confirmed, a little higher). The selector parse is 42% of the build on `compm_22000` (54.6 of 130 M), not 51%. The first selector parse is 3.0% of `compm_22000` and 7% of `rest_13`. It is not the lever.
- Cost of a restyle pass where every element hits the memo: 236 M on `compm_22000` (5.4 K per element) and 31.7 M on `rest_13` (5.3 K per element). About 3 K of it is string work on class names (hash, compare, split, attribute scan).
- Cost of a memo miss: 9.2 K. `compm_22000` has 77,769 misses in 3 passes (89% of the full compute). 82% of the misses end with a style that already exists. The full-style hash (1.5 K) and compare (2.0 K) are paid for nothing in those cases.
- Model: 132,006 element-passes x 5.4 K + 77,769 misses x 9.2 K = 1,429 M. Measured compute plus restyles: 1,406 M.
- Signature sharing (M3) gives 0% on both ramps: all 22,000 matched lists differ. Precise invalidation skips only about 9% of the elements (each div has 6 classes).

### Recommendation

Three parts, in this order, each measured on the whole browser: A class atoms (class and id index keyed by atom, per-element class atom slice), D selector arena with a direct parser, B cascade by winners (second memo keyed by winner values). Estimated saving on `compm_22000`: 506 M (low), 614 M (middle), 781 M (high) against 669 M needed. Only the high case reaches 10x. The middle case gives 9.6x. On `rest_13`: 221 M, 263 M, 340 M against 153 M needed: all cases reach 10x. All gains are estimates. A spike of part A must show 2.7 K or more saved per element before the rest is built. Option H (a lazy style for one element) would remove 77% of `compm_22000` but changes no journey and not `rest_13`. The owner decides.

### Criterion 8: the `cssom-objects` cap

- It protects memory, not an algorithm. `State::roots` in `browser_cssom.rs` gets every CSSOM object that the host makes and never loses one. `deleteRule`, `replaceSync` and a removed sheet leave the roots in place.
- Cost per object after PR #491: 17.8 K instructions and 750 to 960 B for a rule read; 31.4 K and 1,258 B with `.style`; 34.8 K and 839 B leaked for one `insertRule` plus `deleteRule`. A one-rule sheet edited in a loop hits the cap after about 506 K iterations at 494 MiB.
- Recommended design (D1): un-keep the objects that leave a list, prune the host tables when the heap says a handle is stale (`Heap::is_live`), and remove the cap. The JS heap limits (1 GiB, 16 M objects) stay. Tying the cap to the rule count (D2) was rejected: it fails the churn loop sooner.

### Not measured

The journeys. Wall-clock time. Whether a span of the text arena can be reused (needed for part A). Quirks-mode class matching. The Gecko lazy-resolve implementation. Layout inside `rest_13` beyond its call-tree share (about 18.5%).

Kept outside the repo: `/data/bare-tmp/r2/R2-E/` (staged example, counter patch, scripts, profiles).

## R2-C: memory of `python-docs-search-results` after PR #501 (2026-11-14)

Task R2-C of perf goal round 2. Docs only. Design: `docs/design-js-memory.md`.

Question: criterion 6 needs a peak RSS of 92.8 MiB or lower. PR #501 gave 90.3 MiB. Main gives 98.2 MiB. Where did the 8 MiB come from?

Method: 18 merge commits from #498 to `28a8fbc2`, built clean with `base-build`. Recorded corpus, virtual clock, 4 rows each (run 0 with PSS, runs 1 to 3). Machine: archMachine, shared. A second set of builds with a temporary patch (not in the repository) printed live counts. massif gave allocation sites on main. `heaptrack` is not installed. I installed no package.

Results (medians of 4 runs, MiB):

| Merge | Peak RSS | Live bytes in malloc | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #494 | 114.1 | 104.3 to 104.9 | syntax tree of the data literal: 19.4 MiB |
| #501 | 90.3 | 79.2 to 79.6 | the literal is source text: 3.9 MiB |
| #504 | 90.2 | 78.6 to 79.5 | |
| #497 | 97.5 (+7.3) | 84.3 to 84.7 (+5.1 to +5.5) | strings over 32 units are no longer shared: 5.74 M units become 8.61 M units |
| #512 | 95.8 | 84.7 (+0.0) | object record +24 B (+2.3 MiB) against 88.7 K slot `Vec`s removed (about 2.8 MiB) |
| #515 | 97.8 | 85.2 (+0.5) | not examined |
| main | 98.2 | 84.7 | |

- PR #497 explains the growth. The page fetches equal documents several times (`whatsnew/3.14` four times). Each copy is now a new flat string. A forced collect frees 13.5 MiB of them. The collector ran once, because of the 1.75 factor and the 8 MiB minimum.
- PR #512 added no live bytes. Its slab capacity grew by 3.0 MiB and stayed untouched.
- The steps of 1 to 2 MiB after #497 have no change of live bytes behind them. Hypothesis: allocator layout. Not proven.
- Peak split on main (massif, 81.9 MiB live): DOM arena from `DOMParser` documents 22.1 (27%), JS strings 14.0 (17%), object records 12.8 (16%), atoms 8.1 (10%), array elements 7.1 (9%), dictionary properties 5.0 (6%), source copy 3.69, client bodies 3.75, other about 5.4.

Experiments on main (peak RSS, median of 5 runs; MiB):

| Setting | RSS | Instructions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | 97.5 | 2,487 M |
| shared equal text from `Response.text()` | 94.0 | 2,471 M |
| `M_MMAP_THRESHOLD` 256 KiB | 91.5 | 2,484 M |
| both | 85.9 | 2,469 M |
| collect when 8 MiB of flat strings arrived | 94.5 | 2,633 M |
| jemalloc by `LD_PRELOAD` | 121 to 123 | 2,468 M |

Recommendation: build Design 1 (share equal host text, and a fixed mmap threshold of 256 KiB). Expected: criterion 6 at about 86 MiB (-26% against 116). Design 2 (size-class element blocks, inline Latin-1 atoms) is the portable follow-up (about 88 MiB, arithmetic only). Design 3 (free `DOMParser` documents and strings at once) needs a cheaper collector first (one collect costs about 137 M instructions).

The threshold call is glibc only. The fixed threshold costs CPU through page faults: +0.4% to +5.7% on three journeys, +2.8% summed over 47 journeys (loaded machine). Peak RSS summed over 47 journeys: -3.9%.

Not measured: CPU on an idle machine; macOS, Windows and musl allocators; the sharing on the other 46 journeys; XHR `responseText` and `innerHTML` as duplicate sources; Designs 2 and 3 (arithmetic only); test262 and `exec_diff` (no product code changed).

Open questions for the owner are in section 11 of the design document.

## R2-A: where the heavy JS journeys spend instructions (2026-11-14, docs only)

Design: [design-heavy-js-journeys.md](design-heavy-js-journeys.md). Task R2-A of the round 2 plan. No product code changed. Machine-local files: `/data/bare-tmp/r2/a/` (counting profiler, `for-in` and regex prototypes, loop-off patch, profiles, perf data).

Method: main `28a8fbc2`, archMachine (shared), corpus `virtual`, virtual clock. Instruction totals: 3 runs each for `rust-book-search` and `nodejs-org-home` (spread 0.0%), 4 runs for `react-docs` without the loop. Subsystem split: one `perf record -e instructions:u` run per journey with frame pointers. JS-level counts: a counting profiler (patch, 3x overhead; counts and shares only).

Measured split of `rust-book-search` (16,322 M; the loop adds 0 to it):

| Subsystem | Share |
|---|---:|
| Evaluator (tree walker) | 32.3% |
| Regex engine | 25.8% |
| `for-in` key enumeration | 18.0% |
| JS builtins | 9.3% |
| Regex wrapper | 5.2% |
| GC / `JSON.parse` / parse / rest | 9.4% |

Findings:

- `rust-book-search`: 113,523 `for-in` loops examine 6,115,194 prototype keys for 340,317 own keys (all prototype keys are non-enumerable built-in names). 987,649 `RegExp.test` calls run 49,109 different (regex, input) pairs: 95.0% repeat an earlier run. 96.2% of the regex executions are `test()`. 91% of the journey is `makeTeaser` and its callees; the Porter stemmer function of `elasticlunr.js` is 52% (109,398 calls).
- `react-docs`: 16,951 M with the `settle_pictures` loop, 127 to 138 M without it. No lever outside the loop. A lazy image decode (-3.4%) was confounded by the loop and is dropped. One `compare` run gave 4,321 M with the loop off; not explained.
- `nodejs-org-home` (5,921 M, the same with and without the loop): evaluator 75%, parse 6.6%, GC 3.6%, regex compile 1.9%, `for-in` 1.6%. Flat. The register VM lane is not a lever (PR #518: -0.07%).

Prototypes on `rust-book-search` (upper bounds, no invalidation code): `for-in` without the prototype walk 16,322 M to 13,446 M (-17.6%); regex result memo 12,751 M (-21.9%); both 9,861 M (-39.6%, 1.68x against the 16,607 M baseline). Criterion 4 needs 12,774 M or less: the memo alone passes by 23 M only.

Recommendation: D1 (`for-in` stops at a prototype tail with no enumerable key; a count in the shape, or a realm epoch) and D2a (regex result table that charges the stored steps; plus a `test()` wrapper fast path). Estimate: `rust-book-search` about 9.5 to 9.9 G (1.68x to 1.74x), criterion 4 met. Criterion 2: 90.1% to about 84.0% from these two (94,796 M to 88,334 M of 105,189 M); about 79% if the R2-B estimate (-5.4 G) also holds. D2b (a lazy DFA for `test()`) is a later option, estimate only. Nothing for `react-docs` (fix the loop) or `nodejs-org-home`.

Not measured: property gets by kind, string allocations, array growth; live runs; the other 44 journeys; wall time and memory of the prototypes; `size_of::<Res<Value>>()`; the cause of the 4,321 M run; D2b (not prototyped).
Strict formatting fails on unchanged baseline files. Checking an unchanged example from the base reproduces its formatting failure. Strict clippy stops on existing type complexity in the HTML crate. A no-dependencies clippy run also reports existing diagnostics outside the changed logic. These gates are not green. The candidate bare MCP binary passes the local header-echo and protected-route check: status 200, site `same-origin`, mode `cors`, destination `empty`. The installed pre-fix browser sent none of these headers. Both checks used real page JavaScript and a local HTTP server. All owned processes and sessions stopped afterward. No load-test or performance claim is made.
## Textarea innerText collection (2026-11-14)

Issue 482: the rendered-text regression failed with Unsupported before the fix. Rendered textareas now contribute no DOM child text or edited value. Existing whitespace and block boundaries remain. Hidden and detached getter targets retain the DOM-text fallback. The separate select gate remains. No dependency, cache or extra document traversal was added.

All nine element tests pass, including the existing 46-case element fixture. The full bare library run passes 1416 tests with six ignored. The new table cases cover a direct textarea getter, default and edited contents, surrounding whitespace, block display, multiple controls, hidden visibility, a hidden ancestor, a hidden target and a detached target.

Whitespace diff checks pass. Strict rustfmt fails on pre-existing compact formatting; the unchanged base file reproduces the failure. Strict no-dependencies clippy reports 32 existing diagnostics, including unchanged code outside this fix. These two gates are not green. No benchmark or resource claim is made. An isolated candidate with both the metadata and textarea fixes passes the minimal MCP reproduction. SHA-256 followed by body.innerText resolves to the surrounding text, and a later timer resolves. The same candidate receives 200 from the metadata-gated local endpoint. Shared installations stay unchanged.
